items.title: Asda’s £1.2bn equal pay fight enters final legal round
items.summary: Asda faces a potential £1.2bn payout as its equal pay battle enters its final legal stage at the Employment Tribunal this week. The Leeds-based retailer must now prove that pay differences between its store staff and distribution centre workers are justified by reasons unrelated to sex. It follows last year’s Tribunal ruling that store roles [...]
items.body:
Asda’s £1.2bn equal pay fight enters final legal round
Asda faces a potential £1.2bn payout as its equal pay battle enters its final legal stage at the Employment Tribunal this week.
The Leeds-based retailer must now prove that pay differences between its store staff and distribution centre workers are justified by reasons unrelated to sex. It follows last year’s Tribunal ruling that store roles are of equal value to those in distribution centres.
The case involves more than 60,000 Asda workers and is estimated to be worth £1.2bn. In February 2025, the Tribunal found in favour of 12 of the 14 women acting as ‘lead claimants’ for the store staff, ruling that they had established equal value with some of the lead male comparators.
This case has been ongoing since the claim was launched in 2014 and went all the way to the Supreme Court in 2021 over role comparisons, which dismissed Asda’s appeal.
This final stage trial will continue at the Manchester Employment Tribunal until 18 December, with a judgment expected later in 2027.
An Asda spokesperson said: “Asda strongly believes it can defend the pay difference because retail and distribution are two different industry sectors, each with its own market rates and distinct pay structures. It is commonplace to pay market rates in order to attract labour and has absolutely nothing to do with gender.”
Asda equal pay case part of wider retail battle
The hearing is the latest chapter in an ongoing legal battle against major British retailers over claims that predominantly female shop-floor staff are paid less than predominantly male warehouse workers.
Claimant-focused law firms Harcus Parker and Leigh Day are running separate cases against Asda, Next, Sainsbury’s, Morrisons, and the Co-op on behalf of thousands of retail employees, reportedly worth a potential £4bn.
Elsewhere in this sector-wide legal battle, the Supreme Court last month blocked Tesco from appealing a key ruling in its long-running equal pay claim brought by more than 16,000 shop workers.
Tesco had appealed through multiple courts to stop the Tribunal from using a particular definition of ‘work’, before the UK’s top court refused its application.
In September, retail giant Next won an appeal in its own equal pay claim, allowing it to pay warehouse workers more than shop-floor staff.
However, in a statement on the Employment Appeal Tribunal’s decision, Leigh Day called it a “mixed ruling”, noting that the findings that store workers performed work of equal value to warehouse operatives, yet were paid less, remained legally binding.

items.title: Gloomy shoppers are pulling back from buying big ticket items, warns boss of AO World
items.summary: The online white goods retailer cut its annual profit outlook to between £48 million and £54 million, compared to previous guidance of about £54.6 million.
items.body:
Gloomy shoppers are pulling back from buying big ticket items, warns boss of AO World
The boss of AO World said the Budget was ‘an hour of void’ that did nothing to help businesses as the electrical retailer warned over consumer gloom.
The FTSE-250 retailer’s chief executive John Roberts warned customers are pulling back on buying ‘big ticket’ items while the Government has done little to help businesses.
The online white goods retailer cut its annual profit guidance to between £48 million and £54 million, compared to previous guidance of about £54.6 million, sending shares down by 9 per cent on Tuesday.
Roberts said: ‘Interest rates have gone up for the first time in three years. Housing transactions are materially down. Energy bills are going up. Energy security concerns exist. Fuel is going up. They are not the ingredients for a bubbly consumer outlook.’
He said he thought the consumer was not as resilient as AO World was as a business.
Rather than offering businesses any breathing room, Roberts said the Budget last month ‘was an hour of void’ after firms had asked for help with high labour costs.
Shares in AO World tumbled after the group slashed its profit outlook and warned on consumer spending.
He said: ‘The major policy initiatives were conspicuous by their absence. It was a business friendly Budget in the fact that business didn't get punched again.
‘You can't keep going back to business as the cash cow for unaffordable benefits.’
Businesses had been left reeling in previous Budgets after surprise increases to employer National Insurance contributions and wages.
Ministers have since been told these policies have made it harder for businesses to hire, contributing to worrying levels of youth unemployment.
But Roberts said that the Government should make it easier for businesses to decide how to spend apprenticeship levy funding to help solve the crisis of ‘NEETs’ - people not in employment, education or training.
He said the current system was ‘a disaster’ and made it ‘impossible’ to use the funding, meaning ‘the vast majority of it gets returned back to the government in a stealth tax form.’
Firms should instead be given ‘absolute flexibility’ on how to spend the money on apprentices, Roberts said.
His remarks come as other major High Street names, including Lidl and Pret, have urged the Government to immediately implement the youth employment reforms set out in Alan Milburn’s recent review.
Milburn’s report recommended the Government to set a target to double the number of young people completing apprenticeships over the next decade.
Roberts said he felt it was ‘positive’ the report had identified that young people want to work and businesses are keen to hire them.
AO World posted a 20 per cent rise in profits to £21.5 million for the six months to September 30, while sales jumped 6 per cent to £617.5 million.
It has seen sales of energy efficient products increase in the run up to Black Friday, with consumers opting for heat pump tumble dryers to save energy.
It is also expecting to cash in on games such as Grand Theft Auto 6 this Christmas, even though gaming is a smaller part of the business.
Demand for the new release has already been huge. ‘You’ve got grown men taking sick days to play a computer game,’ Roberts said.

items.body:
More than half (55%) of UK shoppers say loyalty offers that are not relevant to them are a major frustration, making them the biggest red flag for retail loyalty programmes. That’s according to new research from HyperFinity, the AI-powered actionable intelligence company.
With retailers competing for customer spending during the crucial Christmas trading period, the findings highlight how poorly designed loyalty schemes risk undermining the relationships they are intended to build. Limited savings (35%), rewards that expire too quickly (29%), and rewards that change or are taken away (25%) are among the other frustrations putting shoppers off.
The findings come from HyperFinity’s Retail Loyalty Index Pulse report, produced with Bloomreach and Eagle Eye. It surveyed 2,000 UK consumers who belonged to at least one of the 51 loyalty programmes featured in the March 2026 Retail Loyalty Index.
Analysis of the findings has identified three key areas where loyalty programmes are falling short of shopper expectations:
- Irrelevant offers: Generic promotions that fail to reflect individual shopping habits give customers little reason to engage with a loyalty programme or return to a retailer. Businesses need to understand what different customers value and make sure the offers they receive are relevant.
- Rewards that fail to deliver value: Loyalty benefits need to offer a clear and worthwhile return. If customers feel the savings are too small, or that spending more does not bring greater rewards, they have little incentive to engage with a scheme.
- Rewards that come with catches: Complicated conditions, short redemption windows and benefits that change or disappear can make schemes feel more difficult to use than rewarding. Retailers should make sure customers can understand, access and redeem the benefits they have been promised.
Thomas Hill, Co-founder and CCO at HyperFinity, said: “Christmas is a critical time for retailers, but it is also when customers have more reasons than ever to compare offers and decide where to spend. A loyalty programme should give people a genuine reason to come back, not just another card in their wallet or app on their phone. That means understanding what different customers value, making rewards relevant and ensuring the benefits on offer are actually worth having. Retailers that get this right have an opportunity to build stronger relationships beyond the festive period, while those that rely on generic offers risk giving customers very little reason to stay.”
To find out more, download a copy of HyperFinity’s Retail Loyalty Index Pulse report here.

items.title: Tesco Winter Food Collection set to boost stocks of essential food items to support communities across UK

items.body:
Tesco customers can make a meaningful difference to the lives of people facing hunger and hardship by donating during Tesco’s 14th annual Winter Food Collection.
Last year, the generosity of Tesco customers enabled 1.48 million meals worth of food to go directly to Trussell and Felix, but support for the charities is needed more than ever.
New research carried out by Felix (formerly FareShare and The Felix Project) found that, of 4,000 working parents sueyed, more than half (53%) struggled to afford food or had skipped food to provide for their children.
While Trussell said food donations to its food banks fell by 22% between 2021 and 2025 and donations for the first half of this year (January to July 2026) were at their lowest level since 2018.
Tesco’s Winter Food Collection, the biggest in the UK, runs in its Express stores from 23rd – 28th November and in large stores from 26th – 28th November.
Pre-packed customer donation bags will be available in stores filled with the most needed items for our charity partners. They are available in all large stores and some of the largest Express stores will also stock them to make donating even easier, no matter where you shop.
The bags, which typically cost between £2 and £4 are pre-filled with healthy and nutritious long-life items and can be picked up in store and paid for at the checkout. The donated food is passed to Felix and Trussell, who will distribute it to charities and food banks to help families who need it most.
The most-needed items according to Felix and Trussell are:
- Tinned fish
- Tinned vegetables and pulses
- Pasta, grains and rice
- UHT milk
Throughout the year, Tesco donates surplus food from its distribution network and stores through its charity and community partners, Felix and Olio. Since 2012, Tesco has donated the equivalent of more than 300 million meals through Felix alone, as part of its Community Food Connection programme.
Ashwin Prasad, Tesco UK CEO, said: “With more families expected to need help with essentials this winter, along with our partners, Felix and Trussell, we are encouraging customers to donate whatever they can to our Winter Food Collection. Food banks and frontline charities need our help more than ever before. Whether it’s in your local store through donating to the Winter Food Collection, rounding up at till, or donating online via our Donr link, even the smallest donation can make a real difference to someone else’s Christmas.”
Matthew Van Duyvenbode, co-chief executive at Trussell, said: “The Tesco Winter Collection is the perfect chance to offer help. The pre-packed donation bags make it easier than ever to support your local food bank. A donation today will make a real difference to your neighbours’ lives. It will ensure people get the emergency food and practical support they need, while we work towards a future where nobody needs a food bank to survive. We are so grateful to Tesco for its continued partnership and to you, our generous supporters, for making someone smile this winter.”
Charlotte Hill, CEO at Felix, said: “Food from Felix reaches a network of over 8,000 charities and community organisations across the UK, helping them to provide food support alongside access to other vital services. Thanks to the Tesco Winter Food Collection we can collect extra stocks of long-life, staple ingredients that complement the fresh surplus food we redistribute. If shoppers can donate just one item at their local store, they’ll be helping to provide a meal for someone facing hardship this winter.”

items.title: Have we lost the art of gift giving? 70% of Brits turn to AI for Christmas present inspiration

items.body:
It seems we’re all getting harder to buy for, and with the influence of social media adding extra pressure on present buying, 68% of Brits say they’re finding Christmas shopping more difficult this year according to a new study by Pandora UK.
Over a quarter (26%) admit they haven’t even started their Christmas shopping yet, and for those that tend to leave it to the last minute, finding the right gift can be a difficult task. Buying Christmas gifts is often considered one of the most stressful parts of the festive season, especially finding the right gift for loved ones – but it’s not due to lack of thought or effort.
Struggling to find suitable gifts isn’t a unique challenge, but the part Brits find trickiest is staying within budget, followed by the challenge of finding something that feels meaningful. We’re not confident in our gift-giving talents either, as almost three-quarters (72%) of Brits admit they’ve worried about a gift not being meaningful enough in the past.
Whether searching for personalised gifts, unique experiences or meaningful jewellery gifting ideas, many Brits are feeling the pressure to find something special.
UK’s biggest gift buying challenges
- Staying within budget (35%)
- Finding something that’s meaningful (24%)
- Choosing something unique (20%)
- Buying for difficult-to-shop-for people (17%)
- Finding time to shop (5%)
Where are we turning with our present-buying woes?
AI platforms have become increasingly integrated into our daily lives in the last year, so 2026 might be the year ChatGPT steps up for present inspiration. According to Pandora’s study, 70% have used or would use AI to help them come up with gift ideas, especially as 11% say that they have more than five difficult people to buy for on their list.
The generation most reliant on AI for present buying is Millennials, with 75% saying they either have or would use a chatbot to help them with their Christmas shopping. That’s compared to just 2% of Boomers who admit to using artificial intelligence for gifting ideas, although 40% of them would be open to using a tool.
Emma Fox, gifting expert at Pandora says “Gift-giving has become increasingly pressured. People want every present to feel personal, memorable and reflective of their relationship with someone, which is why many are turning to AI for inspiration. The worry about using AI is that the results may not feel personal enough, or that it will offer generic options. For those that want to use it, it works best as a starting point rather than a replacement for knowing what makes someone unique.
“The reality is that people value thoughtful gifts. In fact, half of the people we surveyed said that the thought behind a gift is what makes it feel most special to them. Paying close attention to the things your loved ones are interested in and reflecting that in a gift is a great way to do this. That’s why personalised gifts continue to resonate, because they show genuine consideration and thought.”
What makes a present feel meaningful?
- The thought that went into it (50%)
- A shared memory or sentimental meaning (29%)
- Personalisation e.g. engraving (13%)
Only 4% of Brits said that practical gifts felt meaningful, while the money spent was only meaningful to 3%, proving that the most appreciated gifts aren’t always the most extravagant or costly.
How to choose a meaningful gift for a loved one
“If you’ve shared a really memorable moment together, for example taking a special trip or they’ve achieved a personal challenge like a marathon, choosing a gift that commemorates that is always really meaningful and shows thoughtfulness. The key is that it feels personal – maybe referencing a shared joke or memory. Those touches are something AI can’t replicate.
“Personalised jewellery makes a really thoughtful gift and is one of the most meaningful forms of jewellery gifting because it allows you to celebrate memories, milestones and personal connections. Pandora’s new engraving service allows customers to create truly unique engravable jewellery by adding text, drawings or photos to selected pieces.
“From loved ones’ handwriting to children’s drawings or a favourite family portrait, engravable jewellery turns a beautiful accessory into a keepsake that can be cherished for years to come. For anyone looking for personalised gifts this Christmas, adding an engraving can make a present feel even more meaningful.
“Another easy way to get jewellery gifts right is to pay attention to whether they tend to wear gold jewellery or silver, and ensure you choose the type they always wear.”
Top tips for getting gifting right
- Think about their hobbies and passions – then go a step further and think about what they’re missing, problems they might have and how a gift might help
- Choose something that reflects a shared memory that you both enjoyed
- Add considered personalisation where possible, whether through personalised jewellery, engraving or a gift that reflects a shared memory
- Focus on the thought behind the gift over the cost
For shoppers looking for Christmas gifting inspiration, Pandora have shared some of their top suggestions for the festive season below:

items.body:
Alibaba.com, a leading platform for business-to-business (B2B) e-commerce, has named Suleymaan Khan as its Grand Winner of CoCreate Pitch for SuleyNova Robotics, a STEM education brand on a mission to make robotics engineering accessible to everyone.
After a highly impressive pitch, West Midlands-based Suleymaan won $200,0001 for his robotics kit, which offers young people a first route into coding and engineering. Suleymaan’s innovation received glowing feedback from the judges, who described it as being “really impressive”.
Suleymaan is a self-taught robotics engineer and award-winning investor. He built his first remote controlled car at 14 before going on to win the Network Rail Innovation Award in 2023 for his butler robot, “Pepper”. Alongside his business, which he is aiming to scale through partnerships with educational partners and direct-to-consumer, Suleymaan has grown a community on TikTok, sharing everyday stories behind real robotic builds.
Hosted at CoCreate Europe, Alibaba.com’s flagship B2B event, in London on 20th November, CoCreate Pitch saw 20 finalists2 shortlisted from 20,000 global applications. Each finalist had just 90-seconds to present their idea to a star-studded panel of judges, followed by a Q&A, as they competed for the highly coveted grand prize.
In addition to the Grand Winner, Aarav Rao from FreshSense won Silver and was awarded $100,0001 for his artificial intelligence-based product that aims to save perishable foods in fridges, while Italian entrepreneur, Giovanni Tucan, from Clean OS was awarded $50,0001 after claiming Bronze for his product, the world’s first personalised full-arch electric toothbrush.
CoCreate Pitch was the pinnacle of CoCreate Europe, Alibaba.com’s flagship B2B event that returned to London following its inaugural event in 2025. Powered by Accio, Alibaba.com’s plug-and-play enterprise AI agent designed to support the operational needs of SMEs worldwide, CoCreate 2026 brought together thousands of SMEs with industry leaders and field experts to boost the next generation of AI-powered businesses. Unlike standard chatbots that require constant prompting, Accio’s AI agents for e-commerce act as a digital operations team across the business lifecycle, handling market analysis, product design, sourcing, store optimisation and inventory monitoring.
Suleymaan Khan, Founder of SuleyNova Robotics, said: “I feel so passionate about learning how things work and creating tools that can provide young people with practical skills in robotics engineering. This has been the most incredible experience with Alibaba.com. Throughout, I’ve maintained a positive mindset, and manifested that this would happen. Now, I will use this fantastic prize to market and scale SuleyNova Robotics into a business that can empower the next generation of robotic engineers.”
Patrick Sostmann, General Manager Europe, Alibaba.com, said: “This year’s CoCreate Europe has offered SMEs from across Europe a unique opportunity to level-up their businesses through agentic AI for commerce. Agentic AI is unlocking a new era of entrepreneurship that is agile, data-driven, and is highly autonomous, enabling founders to focus on developing new innovations and bringing products to market.”
As we celebrate and recognise some of the best product innovations from across Europe, we’re delighted to have named Suleymaan from SuleyNova Robotics as our Grand Winner this year. His story is inspirational but really this is just the beginning. As young people increasingly seek to enter the robotics and engineering industry, SuleyNova Robotics has huge potential to scale with a difference. We look forward to working with Suley to take SuleyNova Robotics to new heights.”

items.title: Brand loyalty takes a back seat as 87% of employees prioritise discounts

Price is taking precedence over brand loyalty as shoppers prepare for Black Friday, with new research from employee benefits and engagement platform Boostworks revealing that almost nine in ten employees (87%) prioritise the best prices, discounts and offers when deciding where to shop, compared with just 26% who identify loyalty to a trusted brand or […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Price is taking precedence over brand loyalty as shoppers prepare for Black Friday, with new research from employee benefits and engagement platform Boostworks revealing that almost nine in ten employees (87%) prioritise the best prices, discounts and offers when deciding where to shop, compared with just 26% who identify loyalty to a trusted brand or retailer as a key consideration.
The findings also highlight the role workplace benefits can play in helping people make their money go further, with almost two thirds (64%) of respondents, all of whom have access to workplace discounts through their employer, expecting to use workplace discounts, vouchers or cashback on Black Friday purchases.
The survey of employees who use Boostworks’ platform reveals the financial pressures shaping shopping priorities. Almost three quarters (74%) say savings on food and groceries would make the biggest difference to their household budgets, followed by bills, insurance and utilities (52%) and motoring and fuel (38%).
The focus on value is also influencing how shoppers approach Black Friday and Cyber Monday. Three quarters (75%) say they are more willing to switch retailers to secure a better deal than in previous years, while two thirds (66%) plan to compare prices more carefully. Meanwhile, 68% are deliberately waiting for the sales to take advantage of price reductions.
Shoppers look beyond Christmas gifts for Black Friday savings
While 71% intend to use Black Friday and Cyber Monday to buy Christmas gifts, almost as many (67%) plan to make household purchases for themselves, highlighting how shoppers are using major sales events to save money on planned spending as well as seasonal purchases.
Product quality also remains an important consideration for 51% of respondents, although it ranks behind price when deciding where to shop.
Workplace discounts offer practical support beyond Black Friday
With almost two thirds (64%) of respondents planning to use workplace discounts, vouchers or cashback during Black Friday, the findings highlight an opportunity for employers to help their people make savings on purchases they are already planning to make.
And with grocery savings topping the list of areas where respondents would most welcome financial relief, the research also points to the value of making everyday discounts and savings accessible throughout the year, rather than focusing solely on seasonal shopping events.
Jo Werker, CEO at Boostworks, said: “For employers, the message is straightforward. People want benefits that make a difference to their everyday lives, and increasingly that means helping them save money on the things they are already buying.
“Black Friday is a good example of that in action, but the need doesn’t stop when the sales end. When savings on food and groceries would make the biggest difference to household budgets, making discounts, vouchers and cashback easy to access all year round is one of the most tangible ways employers can show their benefits are responding to the financial realities their people face.”

items.body:
Oak Furnitureland has unveiled the latest chapter of its Grow Your Home brand campaign, celebrating the everyday moments that make a house a home, and the furniture that stays with people as life unfolds.
Two films champion the brand’s belief that great-quality furniture should be made to last, becoming part of life’s most precious moments for years to come. The ads, running across TV, streaming, YouTube and social, expand on the promise of stylish furniture built to last a lifetime, backed by Oak Furnitureland’s Lifetime Furniture Guarantee.
Each film follows one piece of furniture through the years. In ‘The Table’, a busy family mealtime gives way to a late-night heart-to-heart between friends, and a dad and his daughter building a den underneath. In ‘The Sofa’, a grandad and his grown-up son doze off after a Sunday roast, a couple settle in for a boxset, and the cushions become islands in a family game of ‘The Floor is Lava’. Years pass, and the furniture is there for every part of it.
The campaign forms part of Oak Furnitureland’s continued investment in strengthening its brand and showcasing its unique proposition of stylish, quality furniture built to last. It comes as the retailer has expanded its offering over the years, diversifying into new categories beyond traditional solid wood cabinetry into a wider range of furniture across dining, bedroom, living and sofas, including ceramic and mixed materials, and its CineLuxe smart-tech sofa collections.
The films, created by TMW, part of Accenture, build on the brand world launched by the agency in 2023, featuring stylish homes set within “the biggest oak tree in the world”.
Since its launch, Grow Your Home has been central to Oak Furnitureland’s customer communications, spanning TV, digital, in-store point of sale and promotional activity.
Alex Fisher, CEO of Oak Furnitureland, says: “At Oak Furnitureland, we believe great furniture should be part of people’s lives for years to come, which is why we introduced our Lifetime Furniture Guarantee.

Leading retail powerhouse Frasers Group today announces a partnership with Visa, a world leader in digital payments, to launch the Frasers Plus Virtual Visa card. The new feature will enable Frasers Plus customers to shop, pay later and earn points wherever Visa is accepted, extending the reach of Frasers Plus beyond the Frasers Plus partner ecosystem for the first time. Points will be redeemable at Frasers Group brands and retail partners including Sports Direct, FLANNELS, Harvey Nichols and Lookfantastic.
This partnership marks a significant milestone for Frasers Plus, combining Frasers Group’s retail ecosystem with Visa’s global payments network to give customers greater flexibility in how and where they spend. Through Frasers Plus, eligible UK customers will be able to:
- Use a single virtual Visa card across Frasers Group brands and anywhere Visa is accepted.
- Spread the cost of purchases through flexible repayment options.
- Earn rewards and unlock Frasers Plus benefits in more places.
- Seamlessly manage payments and rewards through a single account, bill and app.
Developed by Frasers Group Financial Services (FGFS), the Virtual Visa card is a UK market first, bringing retail and consumer finance together in a single, fully integrated product. Purchases made across Frasers Group brands are processed through the Group’s own payment infrastructure, keeping Frasers Plus pricing and rewards in place, while purchases made elsewhere run through the Visa network. For customers, it is simply one card: shop anywhere, earn everywhere.
The card retains the flexibility and familiar account management of Frasers Plus, while delivering a more seamless experience on all Frasers Plus purchases, in-store and online. Powered by Visa’s technology, it takes Frasers Plus from QR code payments to contactless payments through customers’ Apple or Google Wallet. Eligible customers can activate the new feature in the Frasers Plus app by accepting updated terms, with no separate application required. The first phase of the rollout is expected to begin in early 2027.
David Al-Mudallal, chief operating officer at Frasers Group, said: “The introduction of the Frasers Plus Virtual Visa card marks a huge step forward. Partnering with a global leader like Visa to launch this enhanced proposition reinforces our commitment to putting customers first – giving shoppers greater flexibility, more value and more rewarding ways to shop, both across the Frasers Group ecosystem and beyond.”
Ana Reiley, Head of Acceptance, Visa UK & Ireland said: “Working closely with our merchant partners, we know that every retailer’s customers shop differently, and the best payment experiences reflect that. items.body:
Lidl GB is making it easier for shoppers to donate meaningful gifts that offer lasting value this Christmas, with the introduction of brand-new ‘Perfect to Donate’ signage across the Middle of Lidl aisle in 1,000+ of its stores.
Part of the discounter’s Toy Bank appeal, the in-store initiative is informed by Lidl’s first-of-its-kind ‘Price per Play’ index, which identifies the toys that provide the most play for their money – helping shoppers make smarter choices when buying for their own families or donating gifts for those in need.
Launching on 26th November, the new signage will spotlight toys from the top-value categories identified in the index, demonstrating that a toy’s value isn’t necessarily reflected in its price. The ‘Price per Play’ analysis has revealed that traditional staples like books and creative sets provide significantly more long-term engagement than pricier, short-lived items.
To calculate the lifetime value of toys, the index was established by comparing Lidl retail prices with real-world playtime logged by parents across the UK. The formula measures how frequently children return to a toy, the length of individual play sessions, and the total active lifespan before an item is set aside.
Traditional books were identified as the UK’s best-value toy category, costing parents less than 5p per play session and providing an estimated 103 total hours of enjoyment over their lifecycle.
Arts and crafts along with creative and sensory toys (including musical items) rounded out the top three categories, both costing 14p per play session while delivering 95 and 79 hours of active play respectively.
The index also highlights the toys that last the longest and keep children engaged:
- Longest lifecycle: Pretend and role-play toys (such as play kitchens, workbenches, and dress-up sets) remain in active rotation for an average of 175 days – almost half a year.
- Longest focus: Construction and building toys hold children’s attention for the longest single stretch, averaging 80 minutes per session.
- Best durability: A third of parents (33%) identify building blocks as the most durable toys passed down to younger siblings and friends.
Lidl is encouraging shoppers to use the ‘Price per Play’ benchmark when choosing items for its fifth annual Christmas Toy Bank appeal, with key items signposted by the ‘Perfect to Donate’ signage. Shoppers can donate new, unopened toys – of any brand – at collection points across all 1,000+ Lidl stores until 16th December 2026.
Georgina Hall, Director of Corporate Affairs at Lidl GB, said: “Christmas should be a time of joy for every child, but we know many families are facing difficult choices this year. When budgets are stretched, parents want confidence that they’re spending their money on toys children will genuinely enjoy and return to time and again. That’s why we’ve launched our ‘Price per Play’ analysis, which shows that some of the most affordable and traditional toys can deliver the greatest long-term value.
“Our customers have always shown incredible generosity through our Toy Bank, and every single toy donated has the potential to bring real joy to a child. By putting ‘Perfect to Donate’ signs on top toys right in the Middle of Lidl across all stores, we’re making it as simple as possible for our customers to pick up a gift to donate for someone in need.”
Alongside the Toy Bank appeal, Lidl has also stepped in to help ease the squeeze on seasonal shopping, rolling out £25,000 worth of festive food support. Households have one week left to enter for the chance to win a £100 Lidl Plus coupon, which they can either put towards their own Christmas dinner and festive essentials, or extend a helping hand to a friend, neighbour or relative in the spirit of giving. To enter the Prize Draw, customers need to enter their Lidl Plus email address into the form here before midnight Tuesday 1st December.

items.body:
Argos is working with Meta to connect its range of more than 150,000 products with Muse, Meta’s new personal AI agent, launching in the UK today.
By connecting Argos to Muse, customers can ask the AI agent for help with a shopping task, whether that’s finding the right product, comparing options or pulling together a basket. Muse can do the legwork across the Argos website, while the customer stays in control and approves any purchase.
Customers can start with something they have in mind or simply something they want help finding. For example, they could ask which television suits a particular room and budget, choose everything needed for a child starting school, or pull together ideas for Christmas presents within a set price range.
Argos has always embraced new technology to make shopping easier and meet customers where they are. The collaboration with Meta builds on that, exploring how AI can help customers discover and shop its range.
Adam Everatt, director of technology at Argos, said: “Connecting Argos with Muse gives customers another way to enjoy the Argos experience they know and love, alongside our website, app and stores. Whether they’re looking for inspiration or have something specific in mind, Muse offers a new way to explore our broad range, with the convenience and speed they expect from Argos.
Muse, from Meta, lets people create their own personalised AI agent with its own name, look and personality. Muse agents can work across connected apps and services to help people complete tasks, with the user approving before their agent spends, sends or shares.
Shruti Dube, UK country director at Meta, said: “I’m thrilled that millions of Brits will now have access to a personal agent that they control and that gets things done on their behalf. Partnering with beloved British brands and retailers means Muse works seamlessly with services people here use every day, making everything from the weekly shop to sorting out their travel needs easier.”
Customers can choose to connect Argos to their Muse and can disconnect the service through their Muse settings.
Muse is available to anyone aged 18 and over in the UK from today on iOS, Android and muse.ai.

items.title: New study reveals one in three Brits plan to use AI to help with Black Friday shopping this year
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. With Black Friday fast approaching on 27 November, price comparison site idealo has taken a closer look at how Brits plan to shop this year, what discounts they expect and whether Black Friday really offers the best prices. Drawing on a survey of more than 2,000 UK adults and an analysis of over 40,000 daily […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
With Black Friday fast approaching on 27 November, price comparison site idealo has taken a closer look at how Brits plan to shop this year, what discounts they expect and whether Black Friday really offers the best prices.
Drawing on a survey of more than 2,000 UK adults and an analysis of over 40,000 daily prices across 100 popular products and 80 product categories, idealo’s Black Friday Report 2026 explores consumer shopping habits, the growing role of AI in deal-hunting and when shoppers are most likely to find the lowest prices.
The findings reveal that while Black Friday remains a popular shopping event, the biggest savings aren’t necessarily found on the day itself, with many products reaching their lowest prices at other times of the year.
Eight in 10 Brits plan to shop this Black Friday
Black Friday remains a major fixture in the shopping calendar. Two thirds of UK adults (65%) bought something during Black Friday and Cyber Monday 2025, and 80% are interested in shopping this year. Those planning to shop expect to spend an average of £192.
For many, Black Friday is an opportunity to make a purchase they might otherwise put off: almost half (49%) say they are more likely to make a big purchase during Black Friday than at any other time of year.
And shoppers aren’t necessarily waiting for the day itself. More than half (54%) start looking for deals at least a week beforehand. Online marketplaces are the most popular destination (61%), followed by retailer websites (41%) and the high street (30%).
But enthusiasm comes with doubt. Seven in ten (72%) believe many Black Friday discounts are misleading because products aren’t always cheaper than they were earlier in the year, and 62% are more cautious about deals than they used to be. More than eight in ten (81%) say they would trust a retailer more if it showed how its Black Friday prices compared with previous prices.
Christmas gifts and bargain-hunting drive spending
Christmas is the biggest motivation for Black Friday shoppers, with half (50%) of those planning to shop hoping to buy presents at a lower price.
There is also a notable generational difference in how shoppers approach the sales. More than half (55%) of 25-34-year-olds feel pressured to buy during Black Friday in case prices rise afterwards, compared with just 22% of those aged 65 and over.
Younger shoppers are also more likely to hold off purchases in anticipation of the sales: 67% of 25-34-year-olds deliberately put off buying in the weeks before Black Friday, compared with 35% of over-65s.
One in three Brits turn to AI for Black Friday shopping
Artificial intelligence is becoming an increasingly familiar part of the shopping journey, with more than a third of UK adults (34%) planning to use AI tools, including ChatGPT, AI-powered search and retailer chatbots, to help them shop this Black Friday.
The trend is particularly pronounced among younger consumers. Half of 18-24-year-olds (50%) plan to use AI shopping tools, compared with just 14% of those aged 65 and over.
1 in 3 popular products rose in price before their Black Friday “discount last year
While shoppers expect discounts of 24% on average this Black Friday, idealo’s analysis of 80 product categories found that the typical saving on Black Friday 2025 was just 3.4%.
In fact, seven in ten categories saw average prices rise at some point in the six weeks before Black Friday, before falling on the day itself. In some categories, prices remained higher than they had been earlier in October, including speakers (up 26%), external hard drives (up 13%) and VR headsets (up 9%).
The trend was also evident among individual products. Almost one in three (32%) of the 100 popular products tracked increased in price by at least 5% during November before falling on Black Friday. Although their Black Friday prices were 14% lower than their November peak, they were just 1.5% below their October average. For half of these products, there was no saving at all compared with October:
- Apple’s iPhone 13 (128GB) cost £320 throughout October, climbed to £390 for a week in mid-November, then settled at £310 on Black Friday: £80 off its recent high, but just £10 (3%) below its October price.
- Espresso machine (model ES701UK): £500 in October, £640 on 15 November, £539 on Black Friday, which is 8% above its October price.
- Nintendo Switch OLED (Neon Blue/Neon Red): £216 average in October, £240 peak on 26 November, £235 on Black Friday. That’s about 9% above October, but only 2% below its peak.
Categories that were more expensive on Black Friday 2025 than earlier in October 2025:
| Category | Average price, 17 Oct | Average price, 29 Oct | Black Friday (28 Nov) | Black Friday vs 17 Oct | Black Friday vs 29 Oct | 
| Speakers | £323.13 | £317.74 | £407.09 | +26% | +28% | 
| External hard drives | £177.07 | £181.59 | £200.08 | +13% | +10% | 
| VR headsets | £224.31 | £215.59 | £244.69 | +9% | +13% | 
| TVs | £1,079.13 | £1,138.26 | £1,160.80 | +8% | +2% | 
| Hard drives | £189.83 | £192.26 | £201.58 | +6% | +5% | 
| Science & experiment kits | £25.84 | £25.57 | £26.23 | +2% | +3% | 
Source: idealo daily average category prices, 2025.
Black Friday was the cheapest day of 2025 for just six of the 80 categories analysed, while 45% reached their lowest average prices between January and March.
For example, TVs were 25% cheaper in March than on Black Friday. Speakers, VR headsets and deep fryers also reached their lowest prices at other points in the year.
When prices were lowest in 2025 compared with Black Friday:
| Category | Black Friday price | Lowest price of 2025 | Lowest price vs Black Friday | Month of lowest price | 
| TVs | £1,160.80 | £870.69 | 25% lower | March | 
| Speakers | £407.09 | £312.66 | 23% lower | August | 
| VR headsets | £244.69 | £196.29 | 20% lower | June | 
| Deep fryers | £119.05 | £98.72 | 17% lower | January | 
| Espresso machines | £713.70 | £601.29 | 16% lower | October | 
| Women’s jackets & coats | £106.58 | £91.22 | 14% lower | March | 
| Games consoles | £243.22 | £211.42 | 13% lower | March | 
| Mobile phones | £359.30 | £312.68 | 13% lower | January | 
Source: idealo daily average category prices, 2025.
The findings highlight why shoppers should look beyond headline discounts and compare prices over time. A big advertised saving doesn’t necessarily mean a product is at its cheapest.
Katy Phillips, consumer and pricing expert at idealo, says: “Black Friday can still be a great opportunity to pick up a good deal, particularly if you’re shopping for something you’ve had your eye on for a while. We’re not suggesting shoppers should avoid the sales altogether, but rather that they shouldn’t assume Black Friday automatically means the lowest price.
Our research shows that prices in many categories rise in the weeks before Black Friday, meaning an impressive-looking discount doesn’t always represent a genuine saving. The best approach is to do your research, compare prices and look at a product’s price history before making a purchase. That way, shoppers can feel confident they’re getting a genuinely good deal, rather than simply being tempted by a big percentage off.

items.title: Asda faces final showdown in £1.2bn equal pay battle involving 60,000 workers
items.summary: Asda‘s long-running equal pay battle has entered its final stage, with 60,000 current and former employees potentially in line for compensation after more than a decade of legal proceedings. The…
items.body:
Asda faces final showdown in £1.2bn equal pay battle involving 60,000 workers
Asda‘s long-running equal pay battle has entered its final stage, with 60,000 current and former employees potentially in line for compensation after more than a decade of legal proceedings.
The supermarket is back at Manchester Employment Tribunal this week as the final hearing gets underway in a case that could leave Asda facing a compensation bill estimated at up to £1.2bn if the claims succeed.
The hearing, which began on Monday, will run until 18 December, with a judgment expected in early 2027.
Law firm Leigh Day, which represents the workers, first launched the case in 2014, arguing that Asda’s predominantly female shop floor employees were paid less than warehouse workers, who are mainly men, despite carrying out work of equal value.
The latest proceedings will focus on Asda’s material factor defence, which requires the supermarket to demonstrate that the differences in pay were justified by factors unrelated to sex.
The case has already passed two significant legal hurdles.
As reported in February 2025, the Employment Tribunal ruled in favour of 12 out of 14 female lead claimants, finding that their store roles were of equal value to certain higher-paid positions in Asda’s distribution centres.
The ruling covered work carried out between August 2008 and June 2014, although two roles were not found to be of equal value during that period.
It followed an earlier Supreme Court ruling in 2021 that allowed Asda’s shop floor workers to compare their roles with those of warehouse employees for equal pay purposes.
The final stage will now determine whether Asda can legally justify the pay differences, with potential compensation claims depending on the outcome.
Asda has consistently rejected allegations of discrimination.
“Asda strongly believes it can defend the pay difference because retail and distribution are two different industry sectors, each with its own market rates and distinct pay structures,” it told Retail Gazette. “It is commonplace to pay market rates in order to attract labour and has absolutely nothing to do with gender.”
Following the 2025 ruling, an Asda spokesperson said: “We strongly reject any claim that Asda’s pay rates are discriminatory.”
The supermarket maintained that store and distribution roles operated in different employment markets, with separate pay structures reflecting the nature of the work.

items.title: Coca-Cola bottler faces EU probe over claims it blocked supermarkets from cheaper deals
items.summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners is facing a major EU competition investigation over claims it restricted supermarkets from sourcing cheaper drinks across European borders, potentially leaving shoppers paying higher prices. The European…
items.body:
Coca-Cola bottler faces EU probe over claims it blocked supermarkets from cheaper deals
Coca-Cola Europacific Partners is facing a major EU competition investigation over claims it restricted supermarkets from sourcing cheaper drinks across European borders, potentially leaving shoppers paying higher prices.
The European Commission has launched a formal investigation into whether the UK-headquartered drinks giant abused its dominant market position by preventing supermarkets and wholesalers from securing better deals on soft drinks.
Regulators are examining whether Coca-Cola Europacific Partners, which bottles and distributes brands including Coca-Cola, Sprite and Fanta, restricted the movement of carbonated soft drinks and sports drinks between EU countries.
The investigation will look at whether CCEP offered wholesale discounts on the condition that products were not exported to other member states.
The Commission is also examining claims that the business deliberately used different packaging sizes in different countries to make cross-border trading more difficult.
Other allegations include offering incentives to customers to limit imports into Spain and refusing to let supermarket groups negotiate supply deals covering several European countries at once.
If proven, the practices could breach EU competition rules designed to prevent dominant businesses from restricting competition.
CCEP supplies drinks across eight EU markets, including France, Germany, Spain, Portugal and the Netherlands, where the Commission identifies it as the largest supplier of carbonated soft drinks.
European Commission executive vice-president Teresa Ribera said shoppers should not have to pay more for drinks simply because they live in a different EU country.
She warned that restrictions on cross-border purchasing could reduce competition, leaving supermarkets with fewer opportunities to negotiate better prices for customers.
The investigation follows unannounced inspections at CCEP premises in several European countries in March 2025.
CCEP said it took competition law seriously and remained committed to complying with regulations across all its markets.
“We will continue to engage fully with the European Commission’s inquiries,” the company said, adding that it would not comment further while the investigation continues.
However, CCEP posted a 6.5 per cent rise in third-quarter revenue to approximately £4.8bn, with European sales increasing 5.8 per cent.
Its Great Britain business also delivered strong growth, with revenue climbing 9.3 per cent to around £837m, helped by demand for Monster and Powerade.
The company has continued to invest in its product ranges, recently expanding its Supercan offering with new larger-format Sprite, Fanta and Dr Pepper cans.
While the latest investigation concerns CCEP’s activities within the EU rather than its UK operations, the findings could have wider implications for how major drinks suppliers negotiate prices with supermarkets across Europe.
The Commission said it would treat the investigation as a priority, although there is no legal deadline for reaching a decision.
It stressed that opening formal proceedings does not mean CCEP has broken competition law, with the allegations yet to be established.

items.title: ICO fires warning to Meta as Muse AI product launches in UK with Argos and Debenhams onboard
items.summary: Muse, Meta’s new personal AI agent, launches in the UK today, with the likes of Argos, Sainsbury's, JD Sports, and Debenhams Group announcing partnerships.Amid all the buzz and hype, the Information Commission's Office (ICO) has issued a statement and published a blog post reminding developers creat
items.body:
Muse, Meta’s new personal AI agent, launches in the UK today, with the likes of Argos, Sainsbury's, JD Sports, and Debenhams Group announcing partnerships.
Amid all the buzz and hype, the Information Commission's Office (ICO) has issued a statement and published a blog post reminding developers creating agentic AI products for consumers to meet their data protection responsibilities.
Paul Arnold, ICO CEO, says: "We are aware that Meta has launched its Muse AI product in the UK. Agentic AI has significant potential to benefit people and businesses, from saving time on everyday tasks to driving innovation and growth across the economy. For people to benefit from these technologies with confidence, privacy must be built into consumer-facing agentic products from the outset."
"We have been clear with Meta about its responsibilities under data protection law prior to launch, particularly the requirement to ensure that users and the wider public can meaningfully understand and control how their personal data is used in the Muse product."
He adds: "Meta has committed to a voluntary monitoring and reporting scheme with the ICO to ensure we can scrutinise the technology, the user experience and feedback as it is developing. Like any organisation developing or deploying AI agents, Meta is responsible for ensuring that its products fully comply with UK data protection law."
The ICO has set out its initial expectations about consumer facing agentic AI products, as well as the work under way to understand and manage emerging risks from consumer facing AI. It says it is monitoring the roll-out of agentic AI products more broadly and is engaging with major AI developers and deployers to support responsible innovation while ensuring people’s rights are protected.
It has also teamed up with the Competition and Markets Authority to recommend the following steps for anyone thinking about using an AI agent or chatbot.
- Consider the pros and cons: Weigh up the potential benefits and risks of using an AI agent, especially as agents can make mistakes. Mistakes can be magnified if the agent is acting autonomously.
- Check how much the agent can do without asking you: Look for settings that control when the agent needs your approval and remember you can start with the most limited mode. Look for an explanation of what information or tools the agent wants to access, and if permission is for a one-off task or ongoing.
- Know what the AI agent can access and what permissions it has: Understand your settings when signing up and check back in regularly to ensure the permissions and approvals are still right for you.
When it comes to your data:
- Check the privacy controls and default settings: Look at the privacy and data-sharing settings available, including whether your information can be used to train AI or personalise content or advertising. Check what information the organisation says it will use, how it will be used, and what controls you have over this.
- Start with limited access: You don’t have to connect every account or application the agent or platform suggests. Remember you can manage your access permissions on an ongoing basis.
- Look for controls over what the agent remembers: Make sure you understand what information may be stored or retained. If the service offers memory, get familiar with how you can switch off, edit or delete saved information.
- Think carefully about the personal information you directly share or allow the agent to access: including sensitive information about yourself and information about other people.

items.title: Tesco’s robot cleaners sweep into 1,300 more Express stores
items.summary: Tesco is rolling out robotic floor cleaners to another 1,300 Express stores, taking the technology to 1,900 locations. The expansion follows a successful initial rollout across 600 convenience stores earlier…
items.body:
Tesco’s robot cleaners sweep into 1,300 more Express stores
Tesco is rolling out robotic floor cleaners to another 1,300 Express stores, taking the technology to 1,900 locations.
The expansion follows a successful initial rollout across 600 convenience stores earlier this year, with Tesco now bringing the autonomous machines to almost its entire Express estate.
The robots, supplied by cleaning technology specialist ICE, are designed to work alongside store employees, taking care of routine floor cleaning while staff focus on serving customers, replenishing shelves and other shopfloor tasks.
Tesco said feedback from the first 600 stores had been positive, with employees reporting that the machines were easier and less physically demanding to use than their previous cleaning equipment.
The technology also tracks cleaning activity and provides performance reports, allowing stores to monitor whether cleaning routines have been completed.
The latest expansion comes just four months after it was reported that Tesco had completed the first phase of its cleaning robot rollout, which the supermarket and ICE claimed was the largest deployment of its kind in the UK convenience sector.
ICE has been responsible for supplying and servicing cleaning equipment across Tesco’s roughly 2,000 Express stores since 2024, when it expanded its existing agreement with the supermarket.
The decision also forms part of Tesco’s wider push to use technology to take repetitive tasks off staff.
As reported in July, Tesco has been testing autonomous shelf-scanning robots that patrol aisles looking for missing products, misplaced stock and incorrect prices.
It is also introducing electronic shelf labels across its larger supermarkets and Express stores, reducing the need for staff to change paper price tickets manually.
ICE chief executive Mark Bresnihan said the partnership with Tesco showed how automation could work alongside store teams to improve cleaning standards.
It is providing training and maintenance support alongside the machines.
While Tesco has not disclosed how much the expanded programme will cost or how many working hours it expects to save, the move brings autonomous cleaning technology into the vast majority of its UK convenience stores.

items.title: Marks & Spencer looks to hand over 42 European stores to franchise partners
items.summary: Marks & Spencer is reportedly in talks to hand over the running of 42 stores in Greece and the Czech Republic to franchise partners. The company is exploring agreements covering…
items.body:
Marks & Spencer looks to hand over 42 European stores to franchise partners
Marks & Spencer is reportedly in talks to hand over the running of 42 stores in Greece and the Czech Republic to franchise partners.
The company is exploring agreements covering its 27 stores in Greece and 15 in the Czech Republic, as part of plans to grow its international business without taking on the full cost of running stores itself.
Discussions have been underway for some time and could result in agreements early next year.
M&S, which has operated in Greece since 1990 and the Czech Republic since 1996, said it was looking for partners willing to invest in both markets.
The company said: “M&S sees potential for growth in both the Czech Republic and Greece, underpinned by brilliant and engaged colleagues, exceptional product and a trusted brand.”
It added that the discussions formed part of its strategy to grow internationally through simpler, lower-cost partnership arrangements.
The proposed move would see M&S step back from directly managing its stores in the two countries, instead relying on local operators to run the businesses.
No agreements have been finalised, and M&S has not disclosed the identities of the potential franchise partners.
M&S is reportedly hoping to build its overseas presence through franchise agreements, wholesale partnerships and online marketplaces.
The company is also preparing to open its largest international Foodhall in Dubai in December, with more than 3,500 products from its UK food range.
The new store, operated through longstanding franchise partner Al-Futtaim, forms part of a wider Middle East expansion that will see four additional locations open over the next year.
It has also been strengthening its presence in Asia, having signed a new franchise agreement in the Philippines in June.
In August, M&S had expanded its partnership with Zalando’s ZEOS logistics business, allowing it to fulfil online orders across 22 continental European markets while reducing delivery costs.
The changes appear to be paying off.
M&S reported a 22.1 per cent increase in international sales in its latest half-year results, while operating profit before adjusting items rose to £15.3m from £13.3m.
Online and marketplace sales jumped 63.8 per cent, reflecting stronger demand across Europe.
The proposed franchise agreements in Greece and the Czech Republic would mark another step in M&S’s push to expand overseas while limiting the amount of capital it needs to invest directly in stores.
However, the business has not confirmed when the discussions will conclude or whether all 42 stores would be included in any final agreements.

items.title: Aldi cuts product ranges as Lidl takes £23.6m in sales from rival
items.summary: Aldi is cutting back its product ranges across Europe, including the UK, as it hopes to regain ground against Lidl following a sharp slowdown in sales growth. The supermarket is…
items.body:
Aldi cuts product ranges as Lidl takes £23.6m in sales from rival
Aldi is cutting back its product ranges across Europe, including the UK, as it hopes to regain ground against Lidl following a sharp slowdown in sales growth.
The supermarket is removing some branded, niche and duplicate products in favour of everyday essentials and own-label ranges, returning to the simpler, low-cost model that helped it win over shoppers.
The changes are also taking place in Britain, where Aldi typically stocks around 2,000 products.
Lidl is continuing to outpace its biggest discount rival, with sales climbing 6.6 per cent to £3bn in the 12 weeks to 1 November, compared with growth of 0.4 per cent at Aldi, according to Worldpanel by Numerator.
Lidl also took £23.6m in net spending from Aldi during the period, as shoppers increasingly switched between the two chains.
Despite the gap in growth, Aldi remains Britain’s biggest discounter, holding a 10.4 per cent share of the grocery market compared with Lidl’s 8.6 per cent.
The changes are understood to be part of a wider effort to sharpen Aldi’s price advantage over its rivals.
According to Which? research, Lidl was 1.5 per cent more expensive than Aldi on average in the three months to October, while Ocado and Waitrose were 31 per cent and 40 per cent more expensive respectively.
Aldi is now looking to widen that gap further by simplifying its ranges and cutting costs.
Aldi previously made a £100m investment in price cuts across 300 products in July, which formed part of its efforts to attract shoppers struggling with household bills.
However, Lidl has been stepping up its own efforts to compete on value.
As reported last month, Lidl has invested more than £400m in price cuts and promotions this year, including reductions across more than 1,200 products.
Aldi is taking a similar back-to-basics approach in other European markets.
In Italy, it announced plans in September to return to its discounting roots, while its Swiss business has pledged to focus on its core value proposition.
It is also reducing its product assortment in Germany as part of efforts to lower operating costs.
Kearney senior partner Mirko Warschun told the Financial Times that Aldi’s strategy was about refining its existing model rather than changing direction.
He warned that adding too many products risked undermining the simplicity that had made the business successful.
The change to the range it offers comes as Aldi faces another challenge of slowing store expansion.
It had previously targeted 1,200 UK stores by the end of 2025 but currently operates just over 1,000, despite maintaining a longer-term ambition of reaching 1,500 locations.
Aldi plans on investing £900m in its UK operations next year, including plans to open around 40 new supermarkets.
Both Aldi and Lidl are also facing tighter rules around property agreements following a recent decision by the Competition and Markets Authority.
The watchdog ruled last month that the two discounters must face the same restrictions as Britain’s biggest supermarkets, limiting their ability to use land agreements to prevent competitors opening nearby.
Aldi UK defended its performance, pointing to Worldpanel data showing it was the only major supermarket where average prices were lower than a year ago.

items.title: Tesco taps Cisco executive Cheryl Lynch for senior technology role
items.summary: Tesco has appointed former Cisco executive Cheryl Lynch as its new head of technology operating model. Lynch joins Tesco Technology after six years at Cisco, where she held the position…
items.body:
Tesco taps Cisco executive Cheryl Lynch for senior technology role
Tesco has appointed former Cisco executive Cheryl Lynch as its new head of technology operating model.
Lynch joins Tesco Technology after six years at Cisco, where she held the position of senior director. Her previous experience also includes a role at airline Emirates.
Announcing the move on LinkedIn, Lynch said she had started a new chapter at Tesco, describing the position as “a new and exciting role” that felt like the perfect fit.
She also praised her introduction to the business, revealing that she had been set up with her laptop and full system access within 90 minutes of arriving on her first day.
Tesco is continuing to expand its in-house technology capabilities, having doubled its technology workforce over the past six years to more than 6,000 employees across the UK, Ireland, Central Europe and India.
Tesco has been investing in artificial intelligence, automation and digital systems to improve the way its stores and online operations work.
As Grocery Gazette reported in April, the supermarket began testing an AI-powered shopping assistant with 280,000 employees ahead of a planned customer rollout.
The technology is designed to help shoppers plan meals, discover recipes and add ingredients directly to their online baskets.
Tesco also signed a partnership with French AI firm Mistral last year to explore how artificial intelligence could improve internal operations and make everyday tasks easier for employees.
Meanwhile, its investment in store technology has continued, with plans to introduce electronic shelf labels across 3,000 UK stores to reduce the need for manual price changes.
The supermarket has also been trialling autonomous shelf-scanning robots to help identify missing products and pricing errors.
Lynch’s arrival adds further senior experience to Tesco’s technology team as the business looks to manage its growing range of digital services and systems.
Tesco has not disclosed further details about her responsibilities or the projects she will oversee in the new role.

items.title: B&Q owner Kingfisher targets higher profit as Screwfix soars
items.summary: B&Q owner Kingfisher has lifted its profit target for the second time in just two months after seeing its shift towards trade customers drive demand at Screwfix. The FTSE 100 home improvements retailer told shareholders it now expects to notch a pre-tax profit of between £610m and £640m, having lifted its target range to between [...]
items.body:
B&Q owner Kingfisher targets higher profit as Screwfix soars
B&Q owner Kingfisher has lifted its profit target for the second time in just two months after seeing its shift towards trade customers drive demand at Screwfix.
The FTSE 100 home improvements retailer told shareholders it now expects to notch a pre-tax profit of between £610m and £640m, having lifted its target range to between £595m and £635m only in September.
Kingfisher, whose chief executive Thierry Garnier will depart at the end of the year, has looked towards trade customers – including plumbers and electricians – in a bid to grow its sales.
The group said Screwfix, which operates at 943 sites in the UK, has “significantly outperformed the market” in the last three months, helped by growth in its number of customers and the volume of sales.
Kingfisher said growing demand has been driven by its new trade-focused ranges of electrical products, plumbing gear and power tools. The retailer has seen “continued momentum” in its loyalty programme, which was launched in October last year.
On a like-for-like basis, sales at Screwfix grew by 6.9 per cent in the third quarter, better than 5.6 per cent growth in the first half of the year.
B&Q, on the other hand, suffered a one per cent drop-off in like-for-like sales, though this was a softer decline than the 1.8 per cent recorded in the second quarter. Kingfisher said the retailer has seen improving sales of painting products and garden power tools.
Kingfisher boss heads for door
The group posted a 2.8 per cent sales decline in France, where it operates the Castorama and Brico Depot retail brands. The latter has suffered from “weaker demand in building materials and larger project categories,” Kingfisher said.
Analysts at stockbroker Panmure Liberum said the group’s growing sales in the UK are “encouragingly” being backed up by “improving trends elsewhere”.
This reduces Kingfisher’s “reliance on any meaningful French recovery where performance has been resilient given the poor economic backdrop,” they added.
Garnier said: “We delivered a solid quarter, with continued market share gains and strong momentum across our strategic growth drivers of trade, e-commerce and marketplace. This gives us the confidence to upgrade our guidance.”
The Kingfisher chief executive announced his departure in May, after being poached by Dutch supermarket group Ahold Delhaize. He will be replaced by Sebastian Gundel, who had been the boss of German DIY retailer OBI.
Garnier added: “We are building a stronger, more resilient Kingfisher and are well positioned to capitalise on the opportunities ahead.
“I want to thank all our colleagues for the energy and commitment they continue to bring to Kingfisher every day. I am incredibly proud to have been part of that team.”
Shares in Kingfisher dipped by 3.6 per cent in early trading to 376p. The stock has gained nearly 19 per cent in the year to date.

items.title: AO boss: ‘The Chancellor gave Brits £100 off energy bills, I’m giving them £3,000’
items.summary: The boss of AO World has taken on the Chancellor’s energy bill handout with his company’s expansion into solar, which he claims will blow Healey’s support out of the water. John Roberts, chief executive of the electricals retailer, said the group’s launch of solar panels will offer households a full package at £5,500, below the [...]
items.body:
AO boss: ‘The Chancellor gave Brits £100 off energy bills, I’m giving them £3,000’
The boss of AO World has taken on the Chancellor’s energy bill handout with his company’s expansion into solar, which he claims will blow Healey’s support out of the water.
John Roberts, chief executive of the electricals retailer, said the group’s launch of solar panels will offer households a full package at £5,500, below the market rate of £8,500.
Taking aim at the Chancellor’s Budget, which he described as “an hour of not a lot”, Roberts said his company’s new venture will do more to take the pressure off of cash-strapped Brits.
He said: “The Chancellor gave households £100 towards their electricity bill. I’m giving them £3,000 – through the discount relative to market price of what we’re giving them in solar.”
John Healey’s headline announcement at the Budget – a £100 rebate on energy bills for about 20m households – will “run out in about 11 or 12 days – there goes a few billion,” Roberts said.
He added: “I’m not sure [the Budget] dealt with anything. It was an hour of not a lot. Ultimately, if you look at the country through a business lens, we have to be focussed on our cost base as much as we are looking after our people, and we’ve got to do things better at lower cost.
“I want to stay absolutely focused on what I’m in control of, and what I’m in control of is delivering amazing value for customers, and we will continue to do that.”
Shares dip after profit downgrade
AO World will launch in solar panels in the next twelve months, before following this up with EV charging and air conditioning.
This new venture will allow the retailer to use the infrastructure it already has for appliance installations, Roberts said.
“When you look at the narrative of energy security for people, solar is going to become more important for people.
“We are good as an organisation at doing very difficult things in and around people’s homes, doing them to a very high standard, and doing that at scale on a national basis, and so we have that infrastructure all in place.”
AO World, which also operates a mobile network and sells electrical goods, grew its pre-tax profit by a fifth in the six months to the end of September, to £21.5m.
The group saw revenue jump by six per cent to £617.5m and said it is “well-positioned” for Christmas trading, though Roberts said the company has “flagged” to its shareholders a drop-off in consumer confidence in recent weeks.
He said the retailer has seen “a slight deterioration in consumer behavior and consumers trading down on value” in the last six weeks. “We’re just flagging a note of caution for the second half,” he said.
The group lowered its pre-tax profit target to a range of £48m to £54m, having previously said in June that it was on track to meet consensus targets of about £54.7m.
Shares in AO World dipped by more than eight per cent in early trading, to 84.5p, as investors were spooked by the warnings of a softer second half.

items.title: Argos customers can now shop with Muse, as Meta’s personal AI agent goes live in UK
items.summary: Argos is partnering with Meta to connect its range of more than 150,000 products with Muse, Meta’s new personal AI agent, launching in the UK today.Customers can ask the AI agent for help with a shopping task, whether that’s finding the right product, comparing options or pulling together a basket.
items.body:
Argos is partnering with Meta to connect its range of more than 150,000 products with Muse, Meta’s new personal AI agent, launching in the UK today.
Customers can ask the AI agent for help with a shopping task, whether that’s finding the right product, comparing options or pulling together a basket. Muse can do the legwork across the Argos website, while the customer approves any purchase.
They can start with something they have in mind or simply something they want help finding. For example, they could ask which television suits a particular room and budget, choose everything needed for a child starting school, or pull together ideas for Christmas presents within a set price range.
Adam Everatt, Director of Technology at Argos, says: “Connecting Argos with Muse gives customers another way to enjoy the Argos experience they know and love, alongside our website, app and stores. Whether they’re looking for inspiration or have something specific in mind, Muse offers a new way to explore our broad range, with the convenience and speed they expect from Argos."
Shruti Dube, UK Country Director at Meta, says: “I'm thrilled that millions of Brits will now have access to a personal agent that they control and that gets things done on their behalf. Partnering with beloved British brands and retailers means Muse works seamlessly with services people here use every day, making everything from the weekly shop to sorting out their travel needs easier.”

items.body:
Debenhams Group is connecting its brands to Muse, from Meta, as the personal AI agent launches in the UK today.
As a result, shoppers’ Muse agents can browse the websites of Debenhams Group brands including Debenhams, Karen Millen, boohoo, boohooMAN and PrettyLittleThing, and present matching products among the options they find.
Over time, a shopper’s Muse agent can learn more about their preferences to help tailor its suggestions. People choose what their agent can access and control what it remembers. It can also keep watch for changes in price and availability after shoppers close the app, taking on the checking and repeat browsing involved in finding the right item.
When shoppers are ready to buy, they can ask their agent to check out on their behalf. It presents the order details and final total for review, completing the purchase when they approve it.
Dan Finley, CEO at Debenhams Group, says: “Muse’s arrival in the UK is a game-changer. Having a personal shopper in your pocket that understands your tastes and budget has the potential to revolutionise how we discover and buy products."
“Take shopping for a holiday as an example. From the suitcase and sun cream to the clothes, your agent can help find what you need, and to turn inspiration into purchase. It makes shopping across fashion, home and beauty quicker, easier and more personal, which makes it such a natural fit for Debenhams Group. Connecting our brands to Muse builds on our wider investment in technology to stay at the cutting edge of retail innovation, making it ever easier for our customers to be inspired and shop.”
Shruti Dube, UK Country Director at Meta, says: “I'm thrilled that millions of Brits will now have access to a personal agent that gets things done on their behalf. Partnering with beloved British brands and retailers means Muse works seamlessly with services people here use every day, making everything from the weekly shop to sorting out their travel needs easier.”
The move extends the group's work with Meta, which earlier this year saw it become the first UK retailer to launch AI driven checkouts on Meta apps for US customers, available across Karen Millen, boohoo, boohooMAN and PrettyLittleThing.

items.summary: Tesco has marked a major milestone with the opening of its 3,000th UK store in Sunbury-on-Thames on 19 November. The new Tesco Express will offer local customers a convenient shop…
items.body:
Tesco celebrates opening its 3,000th UK store
Tesco has marked a major milestone with the opening of its 3,000th UK store in Sunbury-on-Thames on 19 November.
The new Tesco Express will offer local customers a convenient shop to collect groceries, everyday essentials, bakery products and meal deals.
This store opening has led to 14 new jobs and will offer the retailer’s rapid delivery service, Whoosh, in the future.
The supermarket retailer is on track to open 75 new stores between Match 2026 and March 2027, according to the business.
For the upcoming month, Tesco is set to expand with new Express stores in Milford-on-Sea, Preston, Scarborough and Chorley.
Subscribe to Grocery Gazette for free
Sign up here to get the latest grocery and food news each morning
This is part of the retailer’s growing physical footprint, after recent Express openings in Irvine in Scotland, Seamer in North Yorkshire, Newbridge in Wales and Derry/Londonderry in Northern Ireland.
Kevin Tindall, managing director of Tesco UK Stores, said: “Reaching 3,000 UK stores is a proud moment for Tesco, and we’re delighted to be welcoming customers to our new Sunbury Express.
“Every new store is an investment in the community it serves. Here in Sunbury-on-Thames, that means 14 new jobs, a convenient place to pick up everyday essentials, and great-quality food at fantastic prices. That’s what we’re proud to offer local people.”
This comes as the supermarket retailer previously announced a sale of Czech Republic and Slovakia businesses for £1.5bn to completely focus on its UK estate.
Last month, Tesco also expanded its Clubcard scheme, which allows customers to earn loyalty points when shopping at over 500 new partner brands, including Nike, Boden and Ticketmaster.
