items.body:
Co-op Wholesale and award-winning Walthamstow convenience store – Eat17 – have marked their new five-year partnership with an official opening, complete with product sampling and celebratory decor.
The convenience store, located on 24-26 Orford Road, East London, joins Co-op Wholesale as a Proud To Stock Co-op partner, following fifteen years with Spar.
Located in a prime position on the bustling high street, the former Grocer’s winner of its prestigious award, ‘Best Store in the UK’, is fronted by Eat17’s own fascia plus Proud to Stock Co-op signage. It is fitted out to the highest spec and ranged with Co-op Brand ranges as well as the finest locally sourced and produced items.
With a focus on premium, quality lines throughout, the store owners opted to focus on Co-op’s Irresistible lines from chocolate and biscuits to wine and steak, which perfectly complement the existing range of fine foods and drinks.
Partnership with Co-op Wholesale gives Eat17 access to the full range of Co-op Brand products, encompassing 2,400 SKUs as part of Co-op Wholesale’s extensive portfolio of around 13,000 items including fresh produce, food to go, treats, BWS, frozen, chilled and ambient, which are all popular in a convenience proposition and work well alongside the Irresistible range.
The launch event was well-attended by local shoppers, who enjoyed sampling Co-op Irresistible chocolate and wine as they experienced the refreshed store. Co-op Wholesale colleagues joined the celebrations, who will continue to support the retailer in a true partnership fashion. Teams spanning trading, marketing, seasonal and more are looking forward to working closely with the Eat17 colleagues as it settles into life as a Co-op Wholesale’s partner and beyond.
Ian King, Business Development and Growth Director, said: “We’re thrilled to welcome this unique and brilliant store as a partner to Co-op Wholesale. It’s clear to see why it’s won multiple awards – it truly is impressive. Our Co-op Brand lines look totally at home on the shelves, especially the premium Irresistible products. Shoppers were enjoying sampling the Co-op chocolate and wine on offer, which bodes really well for sales, so we’ve no doubt this store will enjoy a very strong future.”
Directors at Eat17, Chris O’Connor and James Brundle, will continue to operate the store serving the bustling residential area with vital food for now, on the go food and drink solutions, snacks, treats, BWS, fresh, produce and more.
Chris O’Connor, Eat17 Director, said: “Eat17 has always been about bringing great food to our local community and this partnership with Co-op Wholesale gives us the chance to offer our customers even more choice. The Co-op Irresistible range is a fantastic fit for the store, sitting alongside the brilliant independent producers and local favourites that make Eat17 special.
“We want customers to enjoy discovering something a little different when they visit, while also finding great quality and value in their everyday shop. We’re excited to share the refreshed store and new range with the Walthamstow community.”
The new store gives local shoppers access to a wide range of everyday essentials, fresh food and Co-op brand products as well as locally sourced offerings, coffee and pizza, which customers can enjoy on site.

items.title: Household rush to stockpile emergency supplies sends British retail sales soaring
items.summary: Surge fuelled by ‘preppers’ heeding Be Ready campaign’s call for households to have three days of food and water for emergencies Business live – latest updates Retail sales in Great Britain surged last month as the public rushed to buy products including tinned food and long-life milk, after the government issued a warning to stock up in case of a disaster. The Office for National Statistics (ONS) said the volume of goods sold jumped by 0.7% month on month in October, defying economists’ consensus expectations of flat sales, as “preppers” took heed of the government’s Be Ready campaign to hold supplies to last 72 hours to survive a possible extreme weather event, cyber incident or another serious emergency. Continue reading...
items.body:
Retail sales in Great Britain surged last month as the public rushed to buy products including tinned food and long-life milk, after the government issued a warning to stock up in case of a disaster.
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) said the volume of goods sold jumped by 0.7% month on month in October, defying economists’ consensus expectations of flat sales, as “preppers” took heed of the government’s Be Ready campaign to hold supplies to last 72 hours to survive a possible extreme weather event, cyber incident or another serious emergency.
The surge in sales is a welcome bounce back for the industry after a poor September, which the ONS has revised down from a 0.4% fall to a 0.6% fall, fuelled in part by poor online sales of autumn and winter clothing because of unseasonably warm weather.
“Supermarkets have told us that sales of long-life food items such as tinned food and UHT milk were boosted by the government’s Be Ready campaign,” said Grant Fitzner, the chief economist at the ONS.
Food store sales, primarily supermarkets, rose by 0.8% month on month, the fastest rate since the 1.4% rise in April.
Oliver Vernon-Harcourt, the head of retail at Deloitte, said: “Consumers responded to the government’s Be Ready campaign by stocking up on long-life grocery items, which reflects a broader attitude from shoppers to prioritise essentials.”
But Paul Dales, the chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said the jump in household “prepping” could mean slower food sales growth in the coming months.
“The cupboards only need to be stocked once for this, hopefully,” he told clients. “It seems unlikely that households can continue to spend at this rate with a further energy-induced rise in inflation around the corner.”
Separate data last week showed that British shoppers had been stocking up on essentials such as bottled water, tinned goods and hand sanitiser in preparation for possible emergencies.
The ONS also reported that textile, clothing and footwear stores reported a 1.5% month-on-month boost in October. An increase in visits to galleries, and a jump in sales of sports equipment, games and toys, lifted sales across other non-food stores by 3.1% month-on-month, the biggest rise since January.
The total non-food stores category – which includes department stores, clothing, household and other non-food stores – increased by 1.1% month on month in October.
Non-store retail sales, primarily online but also sellers such as street stalls and markets, bounced back too, rising 0.9% as a turn in the weather last month drove sales of autumn and winter ranges.
However, sales volumes of motor fuel fell by 2.2% last month, the steepest rate since April, as prices at the pump rose.
“October’s retail sales have exceeded expectations, despite low consumer confidence and growing pressure on household finances from higher interest rates and inflation,” said Erin Brookes, the European retail and consumer lead at Alvarez & Marsal.
“Retailers will be feeling optimistic as the sector approaches the critical Black Friday and Christmas trading period, with October’s sales growth suggesting consumers are still willing to spend this festive season.
“Despite this positivity, retailers are caught between increasingly price-sensitive consumers and mounting operating costs.”

items.title: Poundland dealmakers brace for crunch weekend to avert collapse
items.summary: The advisers running the sale of Poundland are preparing for a hectic weekend as they review last-ditch offers to pluck the beleaguered retailer from the jaws of collapse. Staff at Alvarez & Marsal, the City advisory firm running Poundland’s sale, expect to work through the weekend to determine whether the small number of bidders proposing [...]
items.body:
Poundland dealmakers brace for crunch weekend to avert collapse
The advisers running the sale of Poundland are preparing for a hectic weekend as they review last-ditch offers to pluck the beleaguered retailer from the jaws of collapse.
Staff at Alvarez & Marsal, the City advisory firm running Poundland’s sale, expect to work through the weekend to determine whether the small number of bidders proposing to buy the retailer can stump up the cash they need before it goes bust.
The discount retailer, which has been a mainstay on British high streets since 1990, has until Thursday to find a new home, before creditors rush in to demand their debts are repaid.
Advisors are understood to be considering three bids to take on the company as a whole, including from Irish firm Martin Property Group and little-known investor Xyra Group Holdings.
Bidders have been told they have until the end of Friday to demonstrate to Gordon Brothers, which owns Poundland, how they would fund their proposals to buy the retailer, sources close to the process told City AM.
These suitors will need to explain whether they will ask Gordon Brothers to continue funding an £85m asset-based loan it has used to prop up Poundland, or propose to refinance it themselves.
Advisers will spend the weekend and the early part of next week reviewing these proposals, before deciding by Wednesday which is their preferred bid. “People will be working through the weekend,” a person close to the process said.
Late bidders could emerge
It is not too late for new bidders to emerge, City AM understands. Late entrants to buy Poundland could come to the table over the weekend or as late as early next week, it is understood, though they would have little time to complete due diligence and provide proof of funds.
“There’s still the possibility for new parties to enter into the mix. There are new parties that are still getting in touch at the moment,” a second person close to the process said.
These bids to keep Poundland trading as a whole company could yet fail, meaning the retailer’s 600 stores, 12,000 staff and its stock would be auctioned off to the host of retail rivals waiting in the wings.
The companies which are understood to be eyeing Poundland stores include Tesco, B&M, Lidl, Iceland, The Range and Poundstretcher.
On Thursday, a moratorium blocking Poundland’s creditors from calling in their debts is set to lapse. This was triggered when the retailer’s management filed a notice to appoint administrators last month.
They extended this deadline last week, giving the retailer 10 extra days to find a new home. The moratorium could be pushed back again, but there would be a “very high bar” for a second delay, sources close to the matter said.
Poundland has been stuck in limbo since Gordon Brothers’s attempts to sell it have gained pace. The retailer’s management and its founder, Steve Smith, had claimed the investment firm was starving it of access to its own funds, preventing staff from restocking its shelves.
Gordon Brothers made about £20m available to Poundland last week and it set to release a bigger payment next week to allow it pay its staff.
But ITV News reported on Friday that the retailer remains unable to access £60m in cash receipts which it has generated from sales, meaning its shelves are at risk of becoming empty during the crucial Christmas trading period.
And last week, business select committee chair Liam Byrne accused Gordon Brothers of “jeopardising” thousands of jobs and “strangling” the retailer’s access to its own funds.
Poundland jobs in spotlight
A collapse of Poundland would be the most significant failure in Britain’s retail sector in years and would strike a blow to Andy Burnham’s pledge to revive the high street.
“The truth is that too many high streets have been left to hollow out, leaving town centres a shell of what they once were,” Burnham said in September. “That must change.”
He has previously called on Gordon Brothers to protect as many jobs as possible. He said last month: “If there was a potential owner to avoid [collapse] that hasn’t been accepted, then the business secretary and I want to know why that is the case.”
Business secretary Jonathan Reynolds is set to meet again with Gordon Brothers next week, after a previous meeting in which the investment firm assured him it would prioritise jobs when finding a deal for Poundland.
The retailer’s owner appeared to have distanced itself from this pledge in the following weeks, as Byrne claimed its boss “refused to say it will prioritise saving jobs” during a two-hour grilling at the select committee.
A spokesperson for Gordon Brothers said: “Funds necessary to support Poundland’s ongoing trading continue to be released. We are assessing multiple bids for the sale of the whole company and we are taking due care to ensure that any successful offer can provide the funds required to acquire the business and see it through to sustainable cash generation.”

items.body:
As Black Friday approaches, research from Criteo, the global commerce intelligence platform, has identified three trends that will shape purchase decisions over the holiday season.
With consumers comparing offers, researching products and increasingly using AI assistants for shopping advice, retailers and brands have more opportunities to make the shortlist in the run-up to the retail sales peak and beyond.
TREND ONE: Earlier research will shape holiday shopping decisions
Price will remain a major consideration this festive season, with 81% of UK consumers saying they are planning to look for discounts and promotions when buying gifts. Yet consumers are researching earlier this year, with many planning their wish lists ahead of the sales. As early as September, 59% had already thought about what gifts they might buy. By the time shoppers are ready to take advantage of an offer, many will have narrowed down their choices.
Retailers and brands should ensure visibility at the discovery and consideration stage to meet consumers early, ideally while they are still weighing up their choices. This understanding of shopper intent will be vital as consumers continue to research and shop for gifts this holiday season.
TREND TWO: AI will have a bigger role in helping shoppers narrow their choices
Whether identifying products or comparing prices, AI assistants are becoming part of everyday shopping for many. Criteo’s research found that 43% of UK consumers would use an AI assistant to help choose a gift, with a further 36% open to the idea. This is creating a new point of discovery for retailers and brands.
While AI will play a greater role in product discovery, separate research from Criteo found that 96% of global consumers still use other channels as part of the shopping journey, including retailer sites and apps. Having already narrowed their options with AI, this presents an opportunity for brands to reach shoppers while intent is high.
TREND THREE: The holiday season will put customer acquisition and marketing efficiency under the spotlight
Black Friday and the wider festive period give retailers a chance to reach new shoppers. Criteo’s research found that 80% of UK shoppers buy from online stores they don’t usually shop with at least sometimes. AI-assisted discovery is another opportunity to reach new, high-intent shoppers: in separate research, Criteo’s early analysis across of its US clients found that visits referred from large language models converted at around 1.5 times the rate of other referral channels.
For brands, measuring new customer acquisition, conversion quality and incremental sales will be particularly important in understanding which activity delivers genuine growth throughout the holiday season.

items.title: Timing is everything: new data reveals the exact days to buy – and avoid – this Black Friday
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Black Friday weekend used to be the wild west of discounts but today it leaves consumers playing a risky game of ‘deal or no deal’ when it comes to getting the best prices. Now, new analysis reveals that shoppers can save more than £85 if they choose the right moment. Gekko Web Services, part of […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Black Friday weekend used to be the wild west of discounts but today it leaves consumers playing a risky game of ‘deal or no deal’ when it comes to getting the best prices. Now, new analysis reveals that shoppers can save more than £85 if they choose the right moment.
Gekko Web Services, part of retail marketing consultancy Gekko Group, analysed average prices of nearly 45,000 consumer electronics products at the UK’s five biggest retailers throughout 2025, revealing the best times to buy during the Black Friday weekend – and when playing the waiting game can cost consumers.
Some small discounts kick in during the week before Black Friday – particularly on smart home devices and vacuum cleaners, with prices down 14% and 8% respectively on the annual averages – equivalent to up to £25. However, Black Friday weekend remains the main event across the majority of products.
Games consoles and smart fitness devices are cheapest on Black Friday itself – and waiting until Cyber Monday will cost shoppers. Prices for games consoles increase by £23, while smart fitness devices are typically £22 dearer – both above annual averages.
Conversely, shoppers seeking a good deal on televisions are better off holding fire until Cyber Monday. While those making a purchase on Black Friday can save up to £70 on the annual average, patience can save them an additional £17 – a total discount of £87.
The Black Friday discounting period offers little for those in the market for a new computer or small domestic appliance. Computer prices were 2% above the annual average in the week before Black Friday, decreasing throughout the weekend to break even on Cyber Monday. While Black Friday is the cheapest day to buy small domestic appliances, prices are still 7% above the annual average.

Consumer warning over Black Friday discounts
Despite the discounts available over the Black Friday period, discounts can often be misleading. While prices for many products fall below annual averages, there are often bigger discounts available during other promotional periods. For example, over Easter Weekend 2025, prices for computers were down 21% in comparison to the annual average – equivalent to around £200.
Easter also yielded the largest discounts on games consoles (5%) and small domestic appliances (4%), while TVs and smart fitness devices were cheaper during July’s Prime Days (8% and 7% respectively).
Wider market pressures squeeze 2026 discounts
Supply chain pressures underpin decreasing discounts. Surging global demand for AI data centre infrastructure has driven up the cost of chipsets and memory components throughout 2026, leaving PC and electronics manufacturers less able to absorb steep seasonal price cuts. Combined with rising UK retail overheads and sluggish non-food sales, retailers are increasingly favouring selective, margin-protected promotions over blanket markdowns.
Daniel Todaro, CEO at Gekko Group, said: “While shoppers can bag a great deal on a new TV, Black Friday no longer offers the mammoth discounts we’ve come to expect. Amid an ongoing cost-of-living crisis, stifled consumer spending, supply chain issues and increasing overheads, many retailers and brands are struggling and this is reflected in the scale of the discounts on offer.
“Many consumers hold off for Black Friday, expecting to nab a bargain on Christmas gifts or upgrade household appliances, but they should be aware of price fluctuations and misleading discounts. When you buy can make a difference, and with average selling prices in some categories increasing and better promotions available at other discounting moments, it is more important than ever that consumers monitor prices to make sure they get the best deals.”

items.title: Repeat shoplifter gets nine months behind bars
items.summary: A man has been sentenced to more than nine months in prison for stealing from a Morrisons Daily store and breaching a criminal behaviour order (CBO) in Nelson, Lancashire. Officers were called to Morrisons Daily on Colne Road earlier in November after reports a man… This story continues at Repeat shoplifter gets nine months behind bars Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Officers were called to Morrisons Daily on Colne Road earlier in November after reports a man had entered the store and stolen three cakes and four tubs of sweets.
CCTV showed the man in the footage to be Najaf Khan, 45, a known shoplifter. He had a CBO in place at the time of the offence, which meant he was not allowed to enter Morrisons Daily.
Khan was arrested at his home address on Stanley Street in Brierfield on Saturday a few days later, on suspicion of one count of theft from a shop and breaching his CBO.
He was charged and remanded on both counts, and had also been on a suspended sentence at the time for previous shoplifting offences.
He appeared at Blackburn magistrates court this week and was sentenced to 40 weeks in prison.
PC Bradley Wheeler, of the Pendle neighbourhood policing team, said: “Khan clearly thought he could continue stealing without being caught, but we were determined to bring him to justice.
“His sentence is the result of a thorough investigation and demonstrates our commitment to tackling repeat offenders. As part of Opertion Vulture, those who repeatedly target local businesses should expect to be identified, arrested and put before the courts.”
Operation Vulture is Lancashire Constabulary’s response to shop theft across the county.
The operation sees dedicated officers undertaking hotspot patrolling, increasing their visibility in targeted areas and creating partnerships with retailers across the county to better share intelligence, get a deeper understanding of retail crime and identify more offenders.

Find a better broadband and mobile deal to slash £429 off your bills ahead of Christmas
Products featured in this article are independently selected by This is Money's specialist journalists. If you open an account using links which have an asterisk, This is Money will earn an affiliate commission. We do not allow this to affect our editorial independence.
A typical household could save up to £429 a year by switching broadband, TV and mobile providers, data shows.
Those with a combined TV and broadband package could slash bills by £171 a year on average just by moving, a study by Which? reveals.
Meanwhile, mobile customers who shift from a handset contract to a SIM-only deal once their phone is paid off can save a whopping £258 a year on average.
These combined £429 average savings are reserved for customers who are already out of contract.
If you haven't looked at your account status for some time, spending five minutes to check whether you're still locked into a contract could lead to huge long-term savings – not just for Christmas.
With energy bills set to increase significantly from January for millions of households, it's vital to look for savings wherever possible.
Natalie Hitchins, of Which? said: 'Loyalty rarely pays when it comes to telecoms.
'With many households facing unavoidable price rises in the new year, broadband and mobile are bills where consumers have real power to keep costs down.'
Bad connection: Compare other providers if you're unhappy with your existing one
Switching from biggest providers offers big savings
If you're with Sky, you might want to 'believe in better' prices elsewhere.
Sky customers with a combined TV and broadband package saved a massive £265 on average by switching, according to the study.
Meanwhile, those on a standalone broadband contract with BT can expect to save £162 by shifting to a better deal.
And when it comes to your mobile deal, if you're on EE you should compare your options – customers can save £161 by switching.

Prices usually increase around April every year.
Checking deals using a price comparison website such as Uswitch* is always a good place to start.
You can enter your details to see the options available in your area. Smaller providers that service particular regions – such as Community Fibre in London or Gigaclear for rural areas – are sometimes cheaper.
Many broadband providers have Black Friday deals on, including Community Fibre, EE, Sky and Virgin Media.
For example, Community Fibre is offering double the speed at no extra cost. Prices start at £19 a month for speeds of 300Mbps (megabits per second).

Is it difficult to switch broadband?
Many broadband customers put off switching because of the perceived hassle.
But Which? says that most households found the process straightforward, with 84 per cent of standalone mobile and broadband customers and 77 per cent of broadband and TV customers saying they found switching easy.
The 'one-touch switch' system means that you should only need to contact your new provider to switch – they'll handle the process with your old one.
What if you're locked into a contract?
The cards are in your hand when you're out of contract, because you won't have to pay exit fees to leave your existing provider.
These costs depend on how long you have left on your contract.
Even if you are stuck, it's a good idea to keep an eye on deals. The larger providers offer to pay your exit fees in the form of bill credit when you switch.
EE and Virgin Media are offering to pay up to £300 to switch, while Sky is offering up to £200.

items.title: Convenience stores more popular than pubs
items.summary: It might come as a surprise, but the UK’s convenience stores are more popular than its pubs, according to new research. Local convenience stores came fourth in the list of the most popular small businesses in a survey conducted ahead of Small Business Saturday on… This story continues at Convenience stores more popular than pubs Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Local convenience stores came fourth in the list of the most popular small businesses in a survey conducted ahead of Small Business Saturday on 5 December.
Only coffee shops, bakeries and restaurants came out ahead of convenience stores. Below them were pubs, hairdressers and specialist food shops.
The research, conducted among 2,000 UK adults, found that more than half of them (56%) have at least one favourite small or independent business in their local area, with almost four in ten (39%) having more than one.
Supporting the local economy is a key motivation for Brits to shop small (55%), while 48% value convenience and 46% good customer service.
It seems Britain’s love for its local independents extends beyond being a customer, with almost half (48%) of UK adults either already running a business or would like to start one, although convenience stores did not feature in this category.
Cafés and coffee shops also top the list of businesses Brits would most like to own (9%), followed by bookshops (7%), restaurants and takeaways (6%), phone and computer repair shops or IT support businesses (6%), and bakeries (6%).
Dan Edelman, general manager of UK merchant services at American Express, which sponsors Small Business Saturday, said: “Small businesses bring character to our high streets, creating connections and helping local economies thrive.
“It’s fantastic to see just how much Brits value their favourite independents. American Express is proud to have backed small businesses for many years, including through our longstanding support of Small Business Saturday.
“As we approach one of the busiest shopping periods of the year, we encourage everyone to show their support by choosing to shop small.”

items.title: How to get a bigger Black Friday bargain: cashback, price matches and gift cards
items.summary: From cashback on what you buy to cut-price gift cards, we offer tips on how to maximise savings on your shopping With Black Friday on the horizon, retailers are already offering discounts, and over the next few weeks you can expect to see more price cuts as they attempt to entice us to open our wallets. It could be a great time to snap up the things on your Christmas list or buy household items you need yourself. And there are ways to maximise your savings on Black Friday – which this year falls on 27 November – by doubling up on discounts, or earning cashback on your purchases. Continue reading...
items.body:
With Black Friday on the horizon, retailers are already offering discounts, and over the next few weeks you can expect to see more price cuts as they attempt to entice us to open our wallets.
It could be a great time to snap up the things on your Christmas list or buy household items you need yourself. And there are ways to maximise your savings on Black Friday – which this year falls on 27 November – by doubling up on discounts, or earning cashback on your purchases.
Assuming you have shopped around for a good price and are sure you really want what you are about to buy, here are some ways you can make the bargain even better.
Cashback
There are many ways to earn cashback – and you can often stack up more than one.
Some of the big banks pay cashback on purchases made with their debit cards, with offers linked to specific retailers. Lloyds, for example, runs the Rewards programme, which has cashback deals with a rolling cast of retailers. Santander has the same type of programme called Santander Boosts and Barclays runs Blue Rewards.
Current deals for Lloyds customers include 14% cashback on purchases from Dyson, 8% on the smart-ring maker Oura and 10% on FatFace. If you take advantage of Dyson’s Black Friday deal for a Ball Animal multifloor cleaner, for example, on top of the retailer’s £100 discount, you will get another £39.20 back when you use your Lloyds card to pay – bringing the price down to £240.79.
Many credit cards have similar offers. Barclaycard Rewards, for example, offers a range of deals with different retailers. You need to register in the app before you can start earning money. It also pays 0.25% cashback on other spending.
Typically you have to activate the deals before you spend money. (If you have just bought something and it is showing as pending on your statement, it might not be too late to do so.)
Before you spend anything, check if you need to shop via a specific link. This will be signposted on your bank’s website or app.
Quidco and TopCashback offer cashback from a large number of retailers, including, at the time of writing, up to 10% from the Lego shop and 5% from Boots. The sites require registration, and cashback is available either when you buy via a link or if you buy a gift card (see below).
You might be able to double up by buying through a cashback site and paying with your bank card.
Barclaycard is offering 4% cashback at Currys, while Quidco has a range of cashback offers at the same retailer, including up to 10% on selected wearable tech. Activate the offer on Barclaycard, then use your plastic to shop via Quidco, and you will get back 14% in total.
Gift card discounts
Quidco and TopCashback also offer cashback on retailers’ gift cards, which means you can benefit from the effective discounts in shops as well as online. Currently, for example, TopCashback is offering 6% back when you buy a Primark card to spend in store.
Another place to look for discounts is your workplace intranet. Many employees are offered cut-price gift cards, or access to special discounts, as a perk. Often you can buy instantly usable vouchers for high street shops at below their face value.
There are similar discount schemes aimed specifically at key workers such as teachers and nurses. These also offer gift cards at below face value.
Health Service Discounts and Discounts for Teachers sell discounted gift cards for 170 retailers, and you can use one to pay for something that is already discounted. Current offers include 5.5% off when you buy a Marks & Spencer card and 11% off one to spend with Adidas.
You cannot use these gift cards to buy via cashback sites – you have to go directly to the retailer. The good news is that you do not need to round up to the nearest £10 but can buy what you need to cover your purchase.
At the time of writing, a GHD Gold hair straightener bundle from Argos has a third off and is reduced to £159. Health Service Discounts and Discounts for Teachers are offering 3% off an Argos gift card, saving you another £4.77 – more than enough for a couple of rolls of wrapping paper.
Price matches
Some retailers offer to match prices being charged elsewhere, and it is worth looking at these if you have a specific retailer you want to shop with. It is also worth keeping an eye on prices after you have made a purchase.
You may live near a John Lewis or like to earn the points you get on its credit card, and if so, its price promise could save you money. It pledges to match the prices being charged by a list of 25 other retailers including Currys, Argos and The Entertainer. John Lewis actively reduces prices to match, but if you spot something it has missed within seven days of making a purchase, it will refund the difference. It does have a caveat for Apple products, and will only match products bought directly from Apple or those sold elsewhere with a minimum two-year guarantee.
AO.com has extended its price match guarantee for Black Friday. It says if the price of your purchase drops on its site or you see it cheaper elsewhere, you can claim back the difference any time up to 23 December.
Several retailers including Argos, Currys and Very have a special Black Friday guarantee on some discounted products that only applies to their prices.
Argos, for instance, says that if something is marked with a “price guarantee”, it will not be reduced further before midnight on 25 December – but if it is, you will get a gift card for the difference. You don’t need to invoke the promise – just make sure you give the right email address when you buy.
At Currys, the promise lasts until 1 December, and you need to register your purchase. Once you have done that, it will automatically let you know if the price drops and will arrange a refund into your bank account.
Very is running its price match until 4 December, and shoppers need to contact its customer services if they see something they have bought being sold there for less.

Tesco is set to offer shoppers something different this Christmas with the arrival of three exclusive festive confectionery products from iconic Polish chocolate brand E.Wedel, available in 141 stores nationwide from 24 November.
The seasonal range, distributed in the UK by strategic partner Golden Acre Foods, will feature dedicated Christmas branded floor-standing display units and includes three limited-edition products available exclusively through Tesco for the festive period.
All three SKUs will retail at £6 RSP, with a special Clubcard price of £5 available throughout the launch period on a WIGIG basis.
Founded in Warsaw in 1851, E.Wedel is Poland’s oldest confectionery brand and one of the country’s most beloved food heritage names. The Tesco Christmas range combines the brand’s rich history with distinctive gifting formats designed to bring something new to the UK’s festive confectionery category.
Available exclusively through Tesco and only for the Christmas season, the range reflects growing consumer demand for limited-edition, internationally inspired products that bring theatre, discovery and differentiation to the seasonal confectionery aisle.
The Festive Range Includes:
Torcik Wedlowski Christmas Edition
Created in 1936, Torcik Wedlowski is one of Poland’s most iconic confectionery gifts. The indulgent wafer cake features layers of peanut and chocolate cream, coated in rich dark chocolate. Traditionally gifted for special occasions and often personalised, selected products in the Tesco Christmas range have been hand-decorated with festive designs, making each piece a unique seasonal gift.
Ptasie Mleczko Chocolate & Orange
Another E.Wedel classic dating back to 1936, Ptasie Mleczko is a nationally loved Polish confectionery famous for its delicate marshmallow centre coated in chocolate. Translating as “Bird’s Milk”, the name refers to something rare and special. Tesco shoppers will be able to enjoy a limited-edition festive recipe featuring layers of chocolate and orange-flavoured marshmallow enrobed in dark chocolate.

items.title: Poundland crisis exposes how a retailer can run out of cash despite millions in sales, insolvency expert warns
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. By Molly Monks F.I.P.A., founder of insolvency specialist Parker Walsh “One of the biggest misconceptions about business failure is that a company collapses simply because it has run out of money. In reality, a business can be generating substantial sales, and may even be reporting an operating profit, but still face a serious cashflow crisis […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
By Molly Monks F.I.P.A., founder of insolvency specialist Parker Walsh
“One of the biggest misconceptions about business failure is that a company collapses simply because it has run out of money. In reality, a business can be generating substantial sales, and may even be reporting an operating profit, but still face a serious cashflow crisis if it does not have enough accessible cash to meet its day-to-day commitments.
“That distinction is particularly important in retail, where cash needs to keep moving. Retailers need money available to pay suppliers, replenish stock, cover wages, rent and other overheads, and meet tax liabilities. It is not enough for money to exist somewhere on a balance sheet – the business needs access to sufficient working capital at the right time to keep trading.
“The latest reports about Poundland bring this issue into sharp focus. ITV News has reported that the retailer has around £60 million in sales receipts in bank accounts which management cannot access without approval from its owner, Gordon Brothers. ITV also reports that around £20 million in funding has been released over the past week, while sales are running 20-25% below target and shortages are appearing across some product lines. Gordon Brothers disputes the suggestion that it is improperly restricting funding and says it continues to release money to support the business.
“What the situation illustrates is how quickly a shortage of working capital can become an operational problem. If a retailer cannot pay suppliers or replenish stock, shelves can become depleted. Customers may take their spending elsewhere, sales can come under further pressure and suppliers may become more cautious about extending credit. This can create a damaging cycle in which weaker trading makes it increasingly difficult to restore confidence and stabilise the business.
“The consequences can extend well beyond the retailer itself. Suppliers may be left with unpaid invoices or uncertainty over future orders, while employees face the prospect of losing their jobs. Smaller suppliers can be particularly exposed if a major customer accounts for a significant proportion of their turnover.
“It is also important to distinguish between profitability and cash generation. Poundland’s managing director has said the business is profitable, but EBITDA – a measure of operating performance – is not the same as cash in the bank. A company can show an improvement in its underlying performance and still struggle to meet immediate obligations if funding is unavailable or payments fall due before cash comes in.
“Any rescue deal therefore needs to be about more than simply finding a buyer or agreeing a change of ownership. It must provide enough working capital to pay suppliers, replenish stock and meet essential costs, giving the business a realistic opportunity to return to sustainable trading. Even a promising rescue plan can be put at risk without sufficient funding to keep the operation running.
“The wider lesson for businesses is that cashflow needs to be monitored just as closely as sales and profit. Directors need to understand what cash is genuinely available, when payments are due and how much funding is needed to keep operating. Suppliers should also look beyond a customer’s size and reputation, keeping a close eye on payment behaviour and their exposure to major customers.
“A familiar name, hundreds of stores and millions of pounds passing through the tills do not guarantee financial security. What ultimately matters is whether a business has the cash and funding arrangements it needs to meet its obligations and keep trading.”

items.body:
Retail sales volumes are estimated to have risen by 0.7% in October 2026. This follows a fall of 0.6% in September 2026 and a rise of 0.8% in August 2026, according to the latest figures from the Office for National Statistics.
Food stores sales volumes rose as supermarkets reported increased sales of long-life items such as tinned goods and UHT milk following government advice, while art galleries and clothing stores also rose on the month.
Sara Hudson, partner at McKinsey & Company, said: “Consumers shopped in October, despite the lure of Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals around the corner. Discretionary categories like non-food stores and clothing rose by 3.1% and 1.5% respectively, with clothing sales likely helped by the shift to colder weather.
“Food sales were also resilient, rising 0.8%. The Be Ready campaign contributed here, with consumers encouraged to add extra non-perishable food and bottled water to their shopping baskets.
“With Black Friday sales in full swing, retailers will soon find out how their holiday campaigns performed. The likely brands and retailers that will win, will be those speaking to both consumers and AI. That means making sure product details, stock information and deals are clear and up to date, so AI tools can find and accurately surface them.”
Oliver Vernon-Harcourt, head of retail at Deloitte, said: “The better than expected performance for retail sales in October provides a reassuring start to the Golden Quarter, particularly against a backdrop of higher inflation and continued pressure on household budgets. Consumers responded to the government’s ‘Be Ready’ campaign by stocking up on long-life grocery items, which reflects a broader attitude from shoppers to prioritise essentials. The arrival of colder weather also encouraged consumers to spend on autumn and winter clothing, and the strong growth for other non-food stores indicates that spending on Christmas gifts has already begun.
“Attention will now turn to the big discounting events across November. The promotional period gives consumers a reason to spend, particularly on some bigger-ticket items. As the Golden Quarter enters its most important stretch, retailers have an opportunity to build momentum into Christmas.”

items.body:
This Christmas, elevate festive celebrations and gift-giving with Strucchi’s versatile and approachable vermouths, Vermouth di Torino Bianco and Vermouth di Torino Rosso created exclusively for Marks & Spencer (RRP £16 per 75cl bottle, 16% ABV). Strucchi is available from 491 M&S stores nationwide as the only vermouth available from the retailer. Whether you are searching for a thoughtful gift for the cocktail lover in your life, a stylish host present, or a showstopping ingredient for festive entertaining, Strucchi offers a taste of Italian heritage wrapped in beautiful illustrations.
Strucchi Bianco
Fresh and harmonious, Strucchi Bianco is crafted through the fortification and aromatisation of Italian white wine. It is characterised by notes of wormwood, thyme, and sage, while a smooth, rounded finish is enhanced by delicate hints of vanilla.
Serves: Delicious in a White Negroni or simply top with soda and lemon peel for a refreshing pour.
Strucchi Rosso
Produced from the same base wines and following the same fortification and aromatisation process, Strucchi Rosso offers a rich and persistent profile. Bright citrus notes of orange intertwined with hints of rhubarb and clove, while cinnamon and caramel bring a warm, spicy finish, alongside its characteristic deep amber hue.
Serves: Excellent stirred into a Negroni Sbagliato, or for a lighter cocktail mix equal parts Strucchi Rosso and Tonic and garnish with citrus peel.
Festive Signature Cocktail Serves
Impress guests this season with these easy to make, festive cocktails designed especially for holiday hosting:
Merry Rosso
A rich, warming Christmas cocktail with bright citrus and seasonal spices.
- Ingredients:
o 50ml Strucchi Rosso
o 30ml Cranberry juice
o Squeeze of fresh orange
- Method: Fill a rocks glass with ice. Add Strucchi Rosso, cranberry juice, and a fresh squeeze of orange. Stir gently.
- Garnish: Orange peel & cinnamon stick.
Winter Bloom
A crisp, refreshing highball bursting with festive orchard fruit and elderflower notes.
- Ingredients:
o 50ml Strucchi Bianco
o 15ml Elderflower cordial
o 50ml Pressed apple juice
o Top with ginger ale
- Method: Fill a highball glass with ice. Combine Strucchi Bianco, elderflower cordial, and pressed apple juice. Top with ginger ale and stir gently.
- Garnish: Apple slice & rosemary sprig.
Heritage & Inspiration
Strucchi takes its name from a pivotal figure in the history of Vermouth di Torino: Arnaldo Strucchi. Born in Canelli (Piedmont), he was a visionary oenologist who, with his 1907 book Il Vermouth di Torino, recognised the need to affirm the authenticity of Piedmontese vermouth at a time when imitations were beginning to emerge. His work laid the foundations for what would later become officially recognised guidelines, culminating in the establishment of the Consorzio del Vermouth di Torino and the introduction of Protected Geographical Indication (PGI, known in Italy as IGP) status.
Today, Strucchi reinterprets this tradition “in the manner of Strucchi” through recipes inspired by his philosophy, while embracing a contemporary spirit tailored to the modern consumer.
In celebration of the partnership with Marks & Spencer, and drawing on the legacy of Arnaldo Strucchi, the labels have been illustrated by Riccardo Guasco, an internationally renowned artist known for his distinctive and instantly recognisable style. The designs pay tribute to the imaginary world of two iconic 20th-century figures who, like Strucchi in the world of vermouth, helped shape drinking culture and the art of mixology in Italy and the United Kingdom.
At the heart of the Rosso label is a reinterpretation of the icon of Domizio Cavazza, widely regarded as the father of Barbaresco wine. In the early 1900s, he played a key role in enhancing and redefining this wine, transforming it into an enduring symbol of Italian excellence.
The Bianco label offers a reinterpretation inspired by Ada Coleman, a pioneering British bartender and the first woman to hold the position of Head Bartender at the American Bar at The Savoy from 1903 through to the 1920s.
Enjoy Vermouth di Torino Bianco and Vermouth di Torino Rosso from Marks & Spencer stores now.

items.title: Tinned food and long-life milk boost retail sales after 'Be Ready' campaign launch
items.summary: People stocking up on long-life food drove retail sales higher October, according to official data.
items.body:
Tinned food and long-life milk boost retail sales after 'Be Ready' campaign launch
- Published
Retail sales rose in October, driven by people buying long-life food such as tinned goods and UHT milk, according to official figures.
Sales volumes were 0.7% higher as people responded to the government's emergency preparedness "Be Ready" campaign, the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said.
The campaign encouraged people to stock up in case of disruption to essential services by severe weather or cyberattacks.
Separate research released last week suggested that while households were stockpiling essentials, they were not panic buying.
The government campaign encouraged people to keep three days' worth of food and water in their homes.
Wet wipes, a torch and cash were also recommended.
Data from retail research firm Worldpanel by Numerator indicated last week that people were stocking up on items including tinned meat, bottled water and hand sanitiser.
The latest official sales figures, external from the ONS add to the evidence that the public has begun stockpiling.
"Supermarkets have told us that sales of long-life food items such as tinned food and UHT milk were boosted by the government's 'Be Ready' campaign," ONS chief economist Grant Fitzner said.
"Meanwhile fuel sales have been recovering from earlier low levels, despite pump prices rising again."
The rise in retail sales last month beat some economists' expectations - they had predicted a slight fall - and the increase came after a 0.6% decline in September.
As well as sales being boosted by people buying essentials, visits to art galleries and clothing purchases were also higher in October.
The boost in sales comes at the beginning of the festive period, which is normally the busiest time of the year for retailers.
Jacqui Baker, partner and head of retail at auditing firm RSM UK, said that "retailers will want to see out the year with some Christmas cheer before consumers batten down the hatches in the New Year as energy costs skyrocket and inflation ramps up further".
Typical energy bills are forecast to go up by Â£443 per year from January, pushing up the pace of price rises.
- Sales of tinned food and bottled water jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch 
  - Published10 November
- Why should I stockpile and what will I need? 
  - Published23 October
Separate economic data released on Friday showed the government borrowed slightly less than economists had expected in October.
Borrowing - the difference between public sector spending and income - was Â£17bn last month, the ONS said., external
Although that was Â£0.8bn higher than October last year, it was below analysts' forecasts of about Â£18bn.
Interest repayments were Â£11.2bn - the highest October debt interest figure on record - and Â£2.8bn more than a year ago.
These repayments have been pushed up by higher inflation, as payments on index-linked government bonds are linked to the inflation rate.
Inflation rose to 3.6% in October, mainly because of higher petrol and diesel prices. The rate has been rising in recent months as the Iran war has driven up the cost of energy and fuel.

items.title: How retail PR gets a product launch covered beyond the trade press
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. A new range wins a supermarket listing and the trade titles report it the same week. Buyers, wholesalers and category managers now know about it. The shopper who will stand in front of the shelf in March has heard nothing. Trade coverage speaks to the people who stock a product for future sales. National and […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
A new range wins a supermarket listing and the trade titles report it the same week. Buyers, wholesalers and category managers now know about it. The shopper who will stand in front of the shelf in March has heard nothing.
Trade coverage speaks to the people who stock a product for future sales. National and regional news speaks to the shoppers who buy it as an end user, and it asks for a different story. Retail PR teams that plan both from the start get more from the same launch. The steps below follow the order in which the retail PR works.
One announcement, two press lists
A national consumer or shopping desk wants to know what is new for the shopper: what the product is, what it costs, where it is sold and from which date. A regional title wants the local fact. That may be the town where the product is made, the new store on the high street, the jobs created or the founder who grew up nearby.
Regional coverage is often undervalued. Ofcom’s News Consumption in the UK 2026 research, published in September, found that 95% of adults use local news and information and that 81% get their local news online.
The practical solution is to prepare two versions of one release. The facts and the quote stay the same whereas the headline and the first paragraph change: the national version opens with the product, the regional version starts with the place.
Getting the release onto the news desk
There are three routes, and most launches use more than one. The first is the team’s own contacts: the journalists who already cover the category and already know the brand. The second is a PR agency with its own relationships.
The third is a press release distribution platform. Using B2Press’s UK press release packages, for example, you can send a release in English over the wire of PA Media, the national news agency formerly known as the Press Association, which national newspapers, digital publishers and broadcasters take copy from. The page includes a sample coverage report from a retail release.
B2Press is an online PR platform that helps distribute press releases in 75+ countries and 24 languages, which becomes useful again when the same launch goes to Ireland or the EU.
Whichever route is used, the release should go out with an image. A news editor working to a deadline rarely has time to ask a brand for a product shot.
Here comes the story
Ofcom’s research shows that 82% of UK adults accessed news online in the past month, ahead of television at 79%. Almost three quarters (73%) reached news stories through intermediaries such as social media, search engines, aggregators and AI tools, and 21% used an AI tool for news. A launch story on a media outlet therefore keeps being found for months after the day it runs, so the details in it have to stay correct: the product name as it appears on the pack, the price, the stockists and the launch date.
Online retail gives a second reason to be exact. The Office for National Statistics (ONS) put the proportion of retail sales made online in Great Britain at 28.8% in September 2026. A reader in Aberdeen who sees a story about a brand from Bristol can order within minutes if the press release says where.
A named spokesperson helps as well. The B2Press Press Release Performance Index 2026 covered 2,150 distributions in 83 countries and 32 languages between May 2025 and June 2026. In that analysis, press releases with a spokesperson quote received 11% more coverage than releases without one. The quote works best when it says something only the brand can say, such as why the product was made or what shoppers asked for.
Timing for the first quarter
Christmas pages were filled long ago. Christmas editorial is planned well ahead, and the launches being written up now belong to the first quarter of 2027.
Two dates set the spring calendar. In 2027, Mother’s Day falls on 7 March and Easter Sunday on 28 March. A product tied to either date needs its release, images and samples ready weeks earlier. Releasing under embargo gives journalists time to prepare without the story appearing before the product is on sale.
The business desks have their own calendar. The ONS publishes retail sales figures every month on dates announced in advance, and on those mornings retail reporters are writing about the figures. A launch sent the day before or the day after does not compete with them.
The same launch in Ireland and the EU
A UK release also covers Northern Ireland. The Republic of Ireland is a separate market with its own national media, prices in euros and often different stockists. An Irish version of the release changes those three things and keeps the rest.
EU markets need more work. The release is written in the local language by someone who knows how news is written there, with the local price, the local retailer and, where possible, a local spokesperson. A direct translation of the UK text usually reads like one.
Planning these versions together with the UK launch costs little. The facts, the images and the approval process are the same. Adding them three months later means starting again.
A listing gets a product onto the shelf, and coverage in trade media shows the industry it is there. National and regional news tells the shopper, and that part of the launch is planned at the same time as the rest.

items.title: B&M accuses Morrisons of poaching staff to copy Halloween and homeware ranges
items.summary: B&M has launched legal action against Morrisons, accusing the supermarket of poaching eight of its employees as part of an alleged campaign to copy its seasonal and homeware products. It…
items.body:
B&M accuses Morrisons of poaching staff to copy Halloween and homeware ranges
B&M has launched legal action against Morrisons, accusing the supermarket of poaching eight of its employees as part of an alleged campaign to copy its seasonal and homeware products.
It claims Morrisons carried out a “longstanding, deliberate and concerted campaign” to recruit its staff and use confidential business information to develop similar products, according to High Court documents seen by City AM.
B&M alleges that Morrisons copied dozens of products from its Halloween and autumn homeware collections, including scented candles, doormats, faux fur throws, duvet covers and decorative accessories.
The case centres on former B&M merchandising director Simon Buckley, who spent more than 14 years with the business before joining Morrisons as trading director for general merchandise in January.
B&M claims Buckley breached the terms of his employment contract by holding discussions with Morrisons while on gardening leave.
It also alleges that he shared confidential information with his new employer, including documents described as “cheat sheets” containing details of B&M’s bestselling Halloween and gardening products.
According to the court filings, seven other employees from B&M’s buying and product teams subsequently joined Morrisons.
B&M claims Buckley helped encourage those moves, allowing Morrisons to benefit from the expertise and confidential information of its former staff.
The discount chain is seeking damages for alleged intellectual property infringement and breach of confidence, arguing that Morrisons has continued selling the disputed products despite being notified of its concerns in October.
Morrisons has rejected the allegations.
A spokesperson said: “While we will not be commenting in detail as court proceedings have now been commenced by B&M, we do not accept the merits of their claim and will be fully defending it.”
B&M confirmed that it had begun legal proceedings, adding that it invests significantly in developing its products and protecting confidential business information.
The claims have not yet been tested in court, and Morrisons has said it intends to defend the proceedings.

items.title: Baileys Chocolate brings £3.50 advent calendar and festive favourites to supermarkets
items.summary: Baileys Chocolate is hoping to win over festive shoppers with its first £3.50 advent calendar, alongside the return of its popular Caramel Whirls and Christmas gifting range. The 90g calendar,…
items.body:
Baileys Chocolate brings £3.50 advent calendar and festive favourites to supermarkets
Baileys Chocolate is hoping to win over festive shoppers with its first £3.50 advent calendar, alongside the return of its popular Caramel Whirls and Christmas gifting range.
The 90g calendar, available at Sainsbury’s and selected supermarkets, contains 24 milk chocolate buttons flavoured with Baileys Original Irish Cream.
It marks the brand’s first move into advent calendars, offering a lower-priced option as shoppers look for affordable Christmas treats.
Baileys Chocolate is also bringing back its Caramel Whirls, which launched last year and combine milk chocolate with marshmallow and caramel.
The treats are available individually for £1 or in packs of three for £2.75, with stockists including Tesco, Sainsbury’s, Morrisons, Asda, Waitrose, Lidl and Ocado.
As Grocery Gazette reported when the Whirls first launched in 2025, the product was introduced as part of the brand’s efforts to attract shoppers looking for more affordable indulgent treats.
Elsewhere, the Christmas collection includes Baileys Original Irish Cream Truffles, priced at £5.25, and a £7 Chocolate Collection Box featuring milk, white and dark chocolates.
The range is completed by a Christmas Tree Truffle Tin and Christmas Truffle Box, both featuring refreshed festive packaging and prices starting at £5.
Baileys Chocolate manufacturer Lir Chocolates has also switched its individually wrapped truffles to recyclable paper packaging, which it says will remove 13,000kg of non-recyclable plastic from the market each year.
The business claims Baileys Chocolate sales grow 52 per cent over Christmas, making the festive period particularly important for the brand.
Lir Chocolates brand manager Ethan Duffey said: “Christmas remains the biggest opportunity for premium chocolate, and our 2026 Baileys Chocolate collection has been developed to help retailers maximise every gifting and self-treat occasion throughout the season.”
The range joins a growing selection of new festive confectionery products arriving in supermarkets.

items.title: UK supermarkets forced to disconnect thousands of fridges in secret cyber operation
items.summary: Britain’s biggest supermarkets have been caught up in a secret nationwide operation to protect tens of thousands of fridges and freezers from hackers, following a series of cyberattacks that have…
items.body:
UK supermarkets forced to disconnect thousands of fridges in secret cyber operation
Britain’s biggest supermarkets have been caught up in a secret nationwide operation to protect tens of thousands of fridges and freezers from hackers, following a series of cyberattacks that have destroyed food stock across Europe.
Major grocery chains have spent weeks disconnecting refrigeration systems from the internet after security researchers discovered a vulnerability that could have allowed hackers to interfere with temperatures.
The operation, which began in late October, involved the National Cyber Security Centre, the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs and the Food Standards Agency, alongside cybersecurity specialists and supermarket IT teams.
Thousands of devices controlling tens of thousands of refrigeration units were taken offline, with some employees instructed to physically unplug internet cables and monitor temperatures manually.
The security flaw was discovered by researchers at Omega Solutions and subsequently investigated by cybersecurity firm Pen Test Partners.
It involved refrigeration controllers manufactured by British company Resource Data Management, whose equipment is widely used across the UK’s food industry.
It followed a string of attacks on supermarket refrigeration systems in Europe, where hackers remotely changed temperatures and triggered defrost cycles, forcing businesses to throw away large quantities of food.
As reported earlier this month, supermarkets across at least seven European countries were targeted, including stores operated by Carrefour, SuperValu, ICA and Delhaize.
Some refrigeration units reached temperatures of 50C, leaving chilled and frozen products unsellable.
The incidents followed an earlier attack on French supermarket chain Intermarché, which affected hundreds of stores in October.
Although UK supermarkets largely escaped those attacks, several British food suppliers were also targeted.
London-based fruit and vegetable wholesaler Langridge Organic reported that six of its 10 refrigeration units had been compromised, while the Association of Independent Meat Suppliers confirmed incidents affecting several members.
RDM has disputed the severity of the vulnerability, arguing that the researchers’ findings involved testing that went beyond normal procedures, including dismantling its hardware.
RDM chief executive Ged Evans said the company had moved quickly to address the concerns, releasing initial security updates and contacting customers with advice on protecting their equipment.
The company said there was no evidence that hackers had exploited the vulnerability in its controllers.
Pen Test Partners said the immediate threat had largely been addressed, although smaller businesses operating refrigeration equipment could still be exposed.
The firm warned that food manufacturers, cold storage warehouses and other businesses further down the supply chain may not yet have received the necessary alerts.

items.title: Morrisons to shut another 36 Daily stores as convenience shake-up continues
items.summary: Morrisons is planning to close another 36 convenience stores, just months after announcing plans to axe 100 Morrisons Daily sites. The supermarket has proposed shutting a further 36 former McColl’s…
items.body:
Morrisons to shut another 36 Daily stores as convenience shake-up continues
Morrisons is planning to close another 36 convenience stores, just months after announcing plans to axe 100 Morrisons Daily sites.
The supermarket has proposed shutting a further 36 former McColl’s stores across the UK following a review of its convenience estate, with consultations now underway with affected staff.
The latest closures represent around two per cent of Morrisons’ 1,700-strong convenience network.
Morrisons said it would look to redeploy as many affected employees as possible into alternative roles elsewhere in the business.
A spokesperson said: “The performance of our company-owned Morrisons Daily convenience stores continues to improve as they benefit from the changes to range, customer service and logistics we have implemented this year.”
However, the supermarket said a small number of stores continued to struggle despite efforts to improve their performance, prompting the latest closure proposals.
The news surfaced just six months after Morrisons revealed plans to shut 100 convenience stores, putting hundreds of jobs at risk.
The affected branches were acquired as part of Morrisons’ £190m rescue of McColl’s in 2022 and had struggled to turn a profit despite attempts to improve trading.
As reported in July, Morrisons began its closure programme with stores in Woodley, Berkshire, and Stokesley, North Yorkshire.
Morrisons previously blamed rising employment costs, including increases to the national living wage and employer National Insurance contributions, for making it harder to turn around underperforming sites.
Despite the restructuring, Morrisons has reported improving sales, with like-for-like revenue rising 3.2 per cent in the 13 weeks to 26 July.

items.title: Supermarket sales jump as shoppers stock up on emergency food supplies
items.summary: Supermarket sales climbed in October as shoppers stocked up on tinned food and long-life milk following the government’s emergency preparedness campaign, helping UK retail sales bounce back ahead of Christmas.…
items.body:
Supermarket sales jump as shoppers stock up on emergency food supplies
Supermarket sales climbed in October as shoppers stocked up on tinned food and long-life milk following the government’s emergency preparedness campaign, helping UK retail sales bounce back ahead of Christmas.
Food store sales volumes rose 0.8 per cent during the month, recovering from a 0.3 per cent decline in September, according to the latest Office for National Statistics figures.
The increase helped push overall retail sales volumes up 0.7 per cent month on month, beating economists’ expectations of no growth and reversing September’s 0.6 per cent fall.
Sales volumes were also 2.3 per cent higher than October last year.
The ONS said supermarkets had reported increased demand for tinned goods, UHT milk and other long-life products following the launch of the government’s Be Ready campaign on 22 October.
The initiative encourages households to keep at least three days’ worth of essential supplies, including food, water, torches and batteries, in case of emergencies such as severe weather or cyberattacks.
ONS chief economist Grant Fitzner said supermarkets had seen a clear increase in purchases of long-life food following the campaign.
The findings confirm a trend Grocery Gazette reported earlier this month, when Worldpanel by Numerator data showed sales of bottled water jumping 67 per cent and tinned and jarred goods rising 37 per cent in the 10 days following the government’s advice.
Hand sanitiser sales also surged 83 per cent, although Worldpanel stressed that shoppers were gradually building up supplies rather than panic buying.
The latest ONS figures suggest the increased demand has provided a boost for supermarkets at the start of the crucial Christmas trading period.
Elsewhere, non-food sales volumes rose 1.1 per cent in October, helped by stronger clothing sales as cooler weather encouraged shoppers to buy autumn and winter ranges.
Online spending also increased 1.5 per cent, taking ecommerce’s share of total retail sales to 29.2 per cent.
PwC UK head of retail Jacqueline Windsor said shoppers had bought more from supermarkets in particular after responding to the government’s advice.
However, she warned that the improvement was uneven across the sector, with clothing businesses continuing to face challenges.
Deloitte head of retail Oliver Vernon-Harcourt said the figures offered a reassuring start to the golden quarter, with shoppers beginning to spend on Christmas gifts.
But the stronger performance comes against a difficult backdrop for household finances.
As Grocery Gazette previously reported, consumer confidence fell sharply in October as rising living costs left shoppers increasingly worried about their finances.
RSM UK head of retail Jacqui Baker warned that businesses would be hoping for stronger festive trading before another squeeze on disposable incomes in the new year.
“Retailers will want to see out the year with some Christmas cheer before consumers batten down the hatches in the New Year as energy costs skyrocket and inflation ramps up further,” she said.

The company presented the move as part of its continuing review of the entire estate and said all the stores being shut were former McColl’s stores, the company Morrisons… This story continues at Morrisons Daily confirms cull of 36 stores Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The company presented the move as part of its continuing review of the entire estate and said all the stores being shut were former McColl’s stores, the company Morrisons took over in 2022.
It also said that the overall performance of Morrisons Daily was getting better.
A Morrisons spokesman said: “The performance of our company-owned Morrisons Daily convenience stores continues to improve as they benefit from the changes to range, customer service and logistics we have implemented this year.
“However, a small number of these stores remain challenged and, as part of the ongoing review of the estate, we have taken the difficult decision to propose closure of 36 former McColl’s stores. These stores represent only 2% of our overall convenience estate.
“Despite significant effort and investment, these locations have remained persistently loss-making in the face of challenging market conditions and increased costs, and we have exhausted all viable commercial options to return them to profitability.
“The decision does not reflect any change in our long-term convenience growth strategy.
“New, modern Morrisons Daily franchise stores are opening every week nationwide and we remain excited about the potential to add hundreds more franchise stores to the network in the years ahead.
“A consultation with impacted colleagues will now commence. Our immediate priority will be on supporting affected colleagues and working to redeploy as many of them as possible into alternative roles elsewhere in the group, in our retail, manufacturing and logistics operations.”
The company announced in May 2026 that it would close 100 company-owned stores.

items.title: Mothercare future hangs in balance after Boots and Middle East blow
items.summary: High street darling Mothercare may be sold or broken up as soon as Christmas after its chair called for a swift end to a strategic review launched to avoid it running out of cash in months. The AIM-listed retailer posted a £2.2m loss before tax in the six months to 27 September, while sales fell [...]
items.body:
Mothercare future hangs in balance after Boots and Middle East blow
High street darling Mothercare may be sold or broken up as soon as Christmas after its chair called for a swift end to a strategic review launched to avoid it running out of cash in months.
The AIM-listed retailer posted a £2.2m loss before tax in the six months to 27 September, while sales fell 14 per cent after a succession of blows to its earnings.
Mothercare lost a key distribution deal with high street giant Boots, and in September warned its future was “highly uncertain” after a Middle East franchise partner shuttered the majority of its stores in the region.
Net debt at the embattled retailer, which sells baby products online and through partners in the UK, ballooned to £9.3m in September, up from £5.8m over the same period the previous year.
Mothercare chair Clive Whiley said the barrage of headwinds had “seriously undermined” the firm’s ability to continue operations.
“Accordingly, although Mothercare has sufficient resources to trade for a number of months, the imperative now is to prioritise discussions to conclude our strategic review of all business and pensions scheme options before the end of the year,” he said.
The group is part-way through a strategic review kicked off after the sudden loss of its Middle Eastern store, which Whiley branded a “heavy blow” when revealing it to shareholders in September.
Mothercare in pension deficit
Alongside the review, the company is locked in a thorny pension deficit negotiations. As part of efforts to turn the under-fire business around, it has not been paying pension contributions, and its pension deficit now stands at £6m.
The business was dealt a further blow by the ongoing Iran war, which has hampered trading in its remaining stores in the Middle East.
Whiley said: “The scheduled closure of the substantial majority of our leading Middle Eastern franchise partners’ franchised stores in the territory in 2027 has seriously undermined our core objectives.”
The company said it was pressing ahead with the appointment of a new franchise partner in the Middle East as one of several last-ditch measures to turn the firm around. It is also engaged in talks with new partners in the UK and has received “expressions of interest” in its intellectual property from overseas.

items.body:
Government stockpiling push helps boost retail sales
Retail sales grew unexpectedly last month as shoppers snapped up stockpiling essentials on advice from the government.
The volume of retail sales in the UK grew by 0.7 per cent in October, despite expectations of flat growth, up from a drop of 0.6 per cent in September, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS).
Rising spending comes amid a slight improvement in consumer confidence. The closely-watched GfK index bounced two points to -22 in November, after falling to its lowest level since Brexit in October.
Last month’s unexpected jump in retail sales was driven by rising demand in supermarkets for “emergency items such as UHT milk and tinned goods,” analysts at the ONS said.
This comes after the government launched its ‘Be Ready’ campaign last month, which urged Brits to build up a three-day supply of tinned food and bottled water in the event of a cyber attack or extreme weather event.
Supermarkets have reported higher spending on long-life products following the stockpiling orders, and tinned tuna maker Princes said earlier this month it has seen “an increase in demand” for its goods.
Non-food sales rose faster than the overall rate, by 1.1 per cent, driven by rising spending on art galleries, sports equipment and toy stores.
The ONS said in-store clothing sales increased in October, as shoppers bought more items per visit after their spending was constrained in September due to “inventory issues” at some big retailers.
Stockpiling boost ‘one-off’
Sandra Prince, head of corporate consumer at Lloyds, said: “While this might be a short-term spike, it shows how quickly shoppers react to changing circumstances. Interestingly, some retailers are now rethinking traditional seasonal stock and moving towards more frequent monthly adjustments to reflect the changing weather conditions.”
But Rajeev Shaunak, head of consumer at consultancy MHA, said October’s stockpiling boost is “probably a one-off which hides the challenges facing retailers as they head into the crucial festive trading season”.
He added: “Squeezed budgets and fragile consumer confidence leave little room for spending beyond the essentials. Black Friday may tempt shoppers to open their wallets, but a rush for discounts is not the same as a recovery in demand.”
October’s pick-up in spending came ahead of a slight recovery in consumer confidence this month, as reported by GfK. Following October’s “dramatic” deterioration, November brought “some welcome relief,” said consumer insights director Neil Bellamy.
He added: “That should reassure manufacturers and retailers ahead of the crucial Black Friday and Christmas trading period that there are still people out there willing to spend. Perceptions of the wider economy have also improved.”
But both GfK’s consumer confidence and purchasing indices remain in deeply negative territory, suggesting that “confidence remains fragile and vulnerable to further economic pressures in the months ahead,” Bellamy said.
