The award follows the
items.body:
Toshiba Global Commerce Solutions and Matalan emerged victorious in the Best Retailer/Technology Supplier Relationship category at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards, recognising the strength of their partnership and the results achieved through Matalan’s in-store transformation.
The award follows the deployment of Toshiba’s VisualStore Commerce Platform and the upgrade of 1,648 tills across 217 Matalan stores to the latest TCx 820 All-in-One POS solution. The transformation moved quickly from pilot to estate wide deployment within six months and was completed at the end of June.
Matalan says that it is experiencing measurable results with a 10% increase in Express Checkout adoption following roll-out and a 55% reduction in hardware maintenance calls, improving reliability for colleagues and customers. The new platform is also enabling it to respond more quickly to changing needs, with recent customer facing functionality developed and deployed in just seven days, without external development support.
The programme created a consistent, flexible technology foundation across Matalan’s store estate while giving its teams greater agility to introduce new capabilities. It also established the foundation for future developments including loyalty, personalised promotions and deeper integration between online and store experiences.
“This award is recognition of what can be achieved when a retailer and technology partner work as one team. From the outset, our focus with Matalan was understanding what its customers and colleagues need and using our retail expertise to deliver meaningful outcomes,” says Martyn Ryder, General Manager UK&I at Toshiba Global Commerce Solutions.
“The results we’re already seeing, just a few months after completing the roll-out, speak for themselves. Matalan now has greater flexibility to innovate and evolve its in-store experience, and we’re incredibly proud to continue supporting them on that journey.”

items.title: Ikea blasts UK business rates burden: check out this week's biggest retail technology stories
items.summary: It's Friday, the weekend is almost upon us, so let’s kick back and reflect on another eventful week for the retail tech space. Here's your briefing on the most important stories from the past few days, including Jysk, Enactor, Sweaty Betty, H&M, Fluent Commerce, REWE Group, Michael Kors, FoundIt
items.body:
It's Friday, the weekend is almost upon us, so let’s kick back and reflect on another eventful week for the retail tech space. Here's your briefing on the most important stories from the past few days, including Jysk, Enactor, Sweaty Betty, H&M, Fluent Commerce, REWE Group, Michael Kors, FoundIt!, Best Buy, Circana, Vusion, and Pricer.
1. Milestone for Jysk as its Enactor powered unified commerce platform hits 2,220 European stores
Jysk reports completion of an important step in its unified commerce journey. All of the retailer's stores in the Netherlands, Belgium, the UK and Ireland are now operating on a new platform powered by Enactor.
With these four countries fully onboard, more than 2,200 Jysk stores have gone live on the platform.
"Our store colleagues are already seeing the benefits," says Melissa Hessing, Store Manager at Jysk Alkmaar. “We moved through it very quickly. The checkout system is very user-friendly and largely self-explanatory. It will be especially easy for new colleagues."
"The implementation has been an exciting and busy process, filled with training, learning and valuable discussions about new ways of working. And there is no doubt that unified commerce will bring significant benefits to our customers, our stores and our colleagues."
2. British activewear brand Sweaty Betty boosts Insiders loyalty programme with Antavo AI platform
Antavo has partnered with Sweaty Betty to revamp its Insiders programme. Powered by the former's AI driven loyalty platform, the omnichannel offering is live in the UK, with Ireland planned for the next phase.
Members earn five points for every £1 spent, whether they shop online, through the app, or in a Sweaty Betty store. They also collect bonus points for joining the programme, downloading the Sweaty Betty app, and following the brand on Instagram and TikTok, with more point earning opportunities coming in the future. Points unlock three tiers: Betty Mover to begin with, Betty Shaker at 1,200 points, and Betty Legend Maker at 2,500 points.
The revamped programme is built around repeat visits. Members earn bonus points for their second purchase and for their first purchase in a store. Milestone rewards add a further pull, with £10 off at the 5th purchase and £20 off at the 10th. The aim here is to shorten time to second purchase, lift purchase frequency and store footfall, and grow CLV and community engagement.
Melissa Mullen, Sweaty Betty President, says :“Our customers have always been at the heart of Sweaty Betty, and our Insiders programme gives us a more meaningful way to celebrate them, whether they shop with us online, in-app, or visit our stores. We’re excited to reward every purchase and every moment of engagement, and we look forward to growing the programme with Antavo as we bring Insiders to even more of our community.”
Insiders is woven into Sweaty Betty’s wider tech stack. mParticle acts as the central customer data platform, sharing member identity and engagement events with Antavo and passing loyalty events on to Braze for tier and programme messaging.
Salesforce Commerce Cloud powers the online experience, NewStore POS brings the programme into Sweaty Betty’s stores, and purchase and return data, down to individual items, flows in through MuleSoft and Antavo’s API.
3. Best Buy teams with Circana to give suppliers a closer look at sales and shopper behaviour
Best Buy is joining Circana’s Gateway programme with a view to giving suppliers a clearer view of how their products sell and how customers shop with the retailer.
Built on Circana's Liquid Data platform and Liquid AI technology, Gateway brings Best Buy's first-party data together with Circana's analytics and AI powered tools in one place. Best Buy’s suppliers will be able to better understand their sales performance and customer behaviour, spot opportunities and make more informed decisions.
“Suppliers want to understand what's happening in a retailer's business, and they want it fast to act on,” says Brad Shelton, President of Global Gateway Solutions at Circana. “With Best Buy Gateway, we're bringing Circana's analytics and AI tools together with Best Buy's data so suppliers can spot opportunities, make more informed decisions and grow together.”
“We have a shared goal with our vendor partners, and that’s to create the best possible experience for our customers,” says Blake Hampton, Chief Merchandising Officer at Best Buy. “Best Buy Gateway allows us to work with our partners to better understand our customers, so together we can deliver even more of what they want and need.”
4. 2027 RTIH AI in Retail Awards opens for entries, winners to be announced at event in London during May
The 2027 RTIH AI in Retail Awards are now open for entries, with our winners being announced during an evening event at The HAC (Prince Consort Rooms) in Central London on Wednesday, 12th May 2027.
The awards celebrate AI innovation in a fast moving omnichannel retail world. It's free to enter and you can do so across multiple categories.
View our 2027 categories and entry forms here.
Key dates for 2026/27
November 2026: Awards open for entries
Friday, 8th April 2027: Awards entry deadline
Tuesday, 13th April: 2027 finalists revealed
Wednesday, 14th April - 28th April : Judging days
Wednesday, 12th May: Winners announced at the 2027 RTIH AI in Retail Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC (Prince Consort Rooms) in Central London
5. Retail sales hit £2.26 billion in FY26 as Ikea UK invests in AI and automation technology
Ikea UK has announced retail sales of £2.26 billion for financial year 2026 (FY26), an increase of 0.5% compared with the previous year (£2.25 billion).
The retailer says that its expanded store footprint helped deliver a strong start to the year, with sales revenue growing 4.7% year-on-year in the first four months of FY26. However, a challenging trading environment with weakened consumer confidence and sustained pressure on household budgets saw sales revenue dip in the second half of the year.
David McCabe, CEO and CSO at Ikea UK&IE, says: “I’m incredibly proud that in extremely challenging market conditions, we’ve managed to close financial year 2026 in growth. In a year when many households continued to manage their budgets carefully, we saw just how important the home remains to people’s everyday lives. This growth reflects the trust people place in Ikea to offer quality, sustainable and well designed home furnishing solutions at prices as low as possible."
“In September, we started financial year 2027 with a clear priority: to continue giving customers the best possible value for money at a time when every pound matters. While cost of living pressures continue, we know a well-functioning home can make a real difference to everyday life. That’s why we’re continuing to invest in lowering our prices, helping more people create the home they want at a price they can afford.”
6. Fluent Commerce starts 2026 with funding news and ends it with H&M deployment
H&M has gone live with Fluent Commerce's Fluent Order Management solution.
A H&M spokesperson described the deployment as moving from "monolithic to composable. From SAP Hybris OMS to Fluent Commerce OMS.”
In a LinkedIn post, Fluent Commerce said: "Delivering that transformation in roughly ten months, while building and scaling a 50+ member team, is a remarkable achievement."
"Huge congratulations to everyone who made it happen. We're proud to be part of H&M’s journey to a more flexible, scalable foundation for the future of their order management and customer experience. Here’s to what comes next!"
7. Vusion preps blockbuster Pricer acquisition as 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards winners agree terms
VusionGroup, a specialist in digitalisation solutions for physical retail, has announced a recommended public takeover offer to acquire all shares in electronic shelf labels big hitter Pricer for SEK 6.00 in cash per share, valuing the company at approximately SEK 980.4 million.
According to a press release, the deal would bring together "two pioneers of electronic shelf labelling solutions, giving Pricer's customers access to a broader range of technology solutions to improve store performance, further digitalise their stores and enhance the customer experience."
The offer has been approved by Vusion's board of directors, whilst Pricer's board of directors has recommended that the company's shareholders accept it.
The acceptance period is expected to commence on or around 8th December and expire on or around 5th January, subject to any extensions. Settlement is set to start on 12th January.
"We are excited by the prospect of bringing together two European pioneers in this sector. Pricer has developed a fantastic customer portfolio of great pioneering retailers across the world and we will put the full strength of our solutions at their service to further improve store performance and the shopping experience," says Thierry Gadou, Chairman and CEO at Vusion.
"Vusion is a key player in store digitalisation solutions with a well established technology platform. We are encouraged by their recognition of the value of Pricer's business, reflected in an offer that provides our shareholders the opportunity to realise the value we have built. The proposed combination could also give our customers access to a broader portfolio of solutions. We are enthusiastic about this opportunity," says Magnus Larsson, President and CEO at Pricer.
8. REWE pulls plug on its Trigo technology powered Pick & Go autonomous store project
REWE Group is ending its Pick & Go autonomous store project. The German retailer has been working on this with Trigo since 2021, tapping computer vision cameras to enable people to shop and go and not have to deal with traditional checkouts.
In a LinkedIn post, REWE Group's Chief Digital & Technology Officer, Christoph Eltze, said: "The future of checkout is not determined by a single technology. A large supermarket has different requirements than a small convenience location or a local supply service. And our customers also have different needs depending on the purchase. That's why we have been testing a wide variety of technological solutions and store concepts for years: from self-checkout and automated checkout processes to largely autonomous stores."
He added: "Our standard is not whether a technology is particularly new or spectacular. What matters is whether it makes shopping easier for our customers and proves itself in real operation. Testing is therefore an essential part of our self-understanding. With clear learning objectives and openness to different outcomes. Because not every test has to be continued exactly as it started. What matters is what we can learn from it and use elsewhere."
In seven Pick & Go test markets in Germany, REWE Group tested computer vision in a day to day store environment over a long period of time. In doing so, it says that it learned a lot about how customers use automated checkout and what requirements the technology must meet in daily operations.
Eltze commented: "We have achieved the learning objectives we set for ourselves in advance. That is precisely why the operational testing phase in these seven markets is now ending, and the evaluation of the insights gained is beginning to decide what further developments we can derive from them."
"What is important to me is that the end of this testing phase is not the end of our engagement with computer vision. On the contrary. We also further test and develop various applications and concepts for automated and autonomous shopping elsewhere. Because it's not about finding a technology for the future of checkout. The goal is to find out which solution offers our customers the greatest added value in which purchasing situation. That's why we test. That's what we learn for. And from that, we continue to develop. This is exactly how reliable decisions are made for tomorrow's trade."
9. First for Loblaw as it ramps up AI shopping experiences push with Meta Muse move
Loblaw Companies reports that it is making its product catalogue available through Muse, Meta's AI powered personal agent.
In doing so, it has become the first Canadian retailer to enable this capability.The announcement builds on Loblaw's recent work to introduce new AI powered shopping experiences.
"Canadians are discovering products and making shopping decisions in more places than ever before, and we want to make sure we're there for them," says Lauren Steinberg, Chief Digital Officer, Loblaw Companies.
"Our work with Meta is about more than adopting new technology. It's about giving customers more choice, better access to the products they need and greater convenience in how they shop. We're focused on using technology in practical ways that deliver real value for Canadians, wherever they choose to shop."
10. 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards winner FoundIt! hooks luxury brand Michael Kors as a new customer
FoundIt! reports that Michael Kors has gone live with its technology. In doing so, the luxury brand says that it has found a solution that solves its discovery challenge and keeps customers exploring when they land on its website.
FoundIt!’s VisNav is automatically guiding customers across the brand's catalogue, with experiences updated nightly to reflect changing shopper intent. When shoppers land directly on a product page from outside (where bounce rates typically reach 65%+), VisNav steps in at the top of the page to keep them engaged and help them find what they're actually looking for.
In a LinkedIn post, Chris Dunn, COO and Co-founder at FoundIt!, said: "What makes this launch especially exciting is the opportunity to help shoppers pick up their journey exactly where they are...turning a product page landing into a more relevant discovery path through the range. A brilliant collaboration with the Michael Kors team, and a great example of navigation doing more than getting people around a site: helping them discover what they came for."
He added: "It's navigation driven commerce in action: Helping customers on their missions; Improving discovery across their product range; Creating navigation that matches shopper intent; Keeping visitors on site when their entry point isn't quite right."
Michael Kors joins the likes of M&S, B&Q, John Lewis, Neiman Marcus, and Saks, who are using FoundIt! to enhance how customers navigate and discover products.

items.title: UK shoppers to spend £6.6 billion this Black Friday but cautious consumption will return in 2027
items.summary: Brits are expected to splash out £6.6 billion on Black Friday this year, with interest in the shopping event and spend rebounding after a dip last year, according to analysis from PwC UK. The recovery, up 40% compared to last year's total of £4.6 billion, comes after in
items.body:
Brits are expected to splash out £6.6 billion on Black Friday this year, with interest in the shopping event and spend rebounding after a dip last year, according to analysis from PwC UK.
The recovery, up 40% compared to last year's total of £4.6 billion, comes after interest in Black Friday also rebounded to 53% after falling to 46% last year when cost-of-living pressures and uncertainty around the budget, affected consumer spend.
The promotional event has divided opinion in recent years with interest hovering around 50% the last few years. Consumers not interested in Black Friday say it's less about affordability than simply not wanting to buy anything, with 40% saying there is nothing they want or need, while 15% are cutting back on spending and 10% say they do not have enough money.
With interest back at more normal levels, average spend on Black Friday is expected to rise to £235 per person, up 24% from £190 per person in 2025. Total expenditure of £6.6 billion is still some way off the record £7.9 billion spent in 2019.
However, this year's Black Friday revival comes amid deteriorating consumer confidence and the prospect of a more challenging start to 2027. PwC’s latest figures show consumer sentiment has fallen from +1 in August to –22 at the end of October, as higher utility bills, higher inflation and the prospect of higher interest rates begin to bite. This is the lowest level since spring 2023.
Sam Waller, Leader of Industry for Consumer Markets at PwC UK, says: “Some analysts say that the Black Friday sales don't matter anymore. Our research tells us that this couldn't be further from the truth. Over half of all consumers are actively looking for a bargain during November, and many of them are buying for themselves rather than cannibalising their Christmas shopping spend. So retailers would be wise to lean into the event to avoid their competitors stealing a march on them.”
“Our analysis shows Black Friday 2026 looks much more like a return to normal after an unusually subdued event last year. While consumer sentiment has softened heading into retail’s Golden Quarter, there is a greater sense of certainty among both consumers and retailers compared to last year. The good news for retailers is consumers say they are protecting their budgets to treat themselves this festive season despite ongoing economic pressures.”
The majority of Black Friday shopping will be done online with over two-thirds of spending taking place online for delivery and 10% for Click and Collect. The rest of Black Friday spending (21%) will take place in-store. The analysis shows that younger shoppers prefer to shop in person, with a third of 18 to 24 year olds and a quarter of 25 to 34 year olds both scoring above the nationwide average.
For retailers, the research points to contrasting trading conditions either side of Christmas. The rebound in Black Friday participation and planned spend presents an opportunity to capture consumer demand in the run-up to the festive period. However, falling confidence and continued pressure on household finances point to a more challenging start to 2027, increasing the importance of how retailers plan for and respond to changing consumer demand.
Jacqueline Windsor, Head of Retail at PwC UK, says: “Shoppers are still planning to spend on Black Friday, and retailers should make the most of it. Health and beauty has been a standout, with notable growth. But the real test for retailers and consumers alike will come in January, when the anticipated ‘credit card hangover’ hits just as costs start rising again."
“In this environment, retailers need to be pragmatic and flexible: capitalise on the appetite to spend now, but plan for a tougher start to the new year. For consumers, it's a season of cautious optimism, with the urge to treat themselves tempered by the reality of tight wallets."

items.title: Retail technology innovation of the week: hologram powered Hunger Games prequel experience launches Stateside
items.summary: Retail Technology Innovation of the Week is a series brought to you by RTIH, highlighting stand out deployments, launches, and initiatives by retailers and tech suppliers.Every week, we showcase forward thinking tech plays that have impressed our Editor and the Retail Technology Innovations Report j
items.body:
Retail Technology Innovation of the Week is a series brought to you by RTIH, highlighting stand out deployments, launches, and initiatives by retailers and tech suppliers.
Every week, we showcase forward thinking tech plays that have impressed our Editor and the Retail Technology Innovations Report judging panel, building up to the publication of the 2026 report later this year.
And this week we’re focusing on Lionsgate and a The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping hologram experience that debuted in premium shopping destinations and movie theatres across the US on Thursday.
Partnering with Hologram Media Network (HMN) and Pretty Big Monster, an UNFOLD company (PBM), the campaign has officially rolled out at over 75 locations, and will be in market through to 30th November, leading into the film’s release in theatres on 20th November.
The interactive activation will bring holograms of two of The Hunger Games’ best known characters, Haymitch Abernathy and Effie Trinket, portrayed by Joseph Zada and Elle Fanning, to theatres, giving audiences a chance to come face-to-face with the film’s leading stars.
Filmed with the cast on set, the experience uses real-time AI transformation technology, shown on Proto Hologram displays via the Hologram Media Network. The campaign will roll-out across all of HMN’s current locations nationwide, with an additional 15 pop-up screens placed in theatres.
“We believe the most memorable experiences happen when people encounter something extraordinary in the places they already go to shop, see a movie or spend time together,” says Andrew Felts, CEO and Founder at Hologram Media Network. “With The Hunger Games, we’re bringing an experience typically reserved for a premiere into those everyday places nationwide, giving fans a chance to step into the story and leave with a memory worth sharing.”
And honourable mentions this week to...
Hotel Chocolat
Hotel Chocolat has launched an AI powered Gift Assistant on its website.
This builds on the retailer's wider Christmas campaign, which starts with the person receiving the gift. A customer could ask, “find me a dark chocolate Christmas gift”. The assistant would then ask a follow up question and refine the shortlist as the customer shares more. From there, the customer can explore product details, choose from available pack sizes and gifting options, and add their selection to their basket.
Hotel Chocolat worked with Astound Digital and Salesforce on this. Salesforce Agentforce and Cimulate’s semantic search capability interpret a customer’s request and match it to product data in Salesforce Commerce Cloud. A customer can start with “a thank you for a host who loves dark chocolate”, refine the recommendations by adding a budget, then choose from available gifting options and add their selection to their basket within the same experience.
Martin Bell, Digital Director at Hotel Chocolat, says: “Search is becoming more conversational, and that’s changing what customers expect from a retailer’s website. We wanted to be on the front foot and make hotelchocolat.com a place people come for expert advice, inspiration and the confidence to choose a gift that feels right."
"In 11 weeks, together with Astound and Salesforce, we transformed the website experience with our new Gift Assistant, in time for our busiest gifting period. That means we can learn from real Christmas shopping decisions by seeing what people ask for, which recommendations they act on and where they still need help. What we learn will shape how we use conversational AI across Hotel Chocolat, including how we help customers discover our products when their search starts beyond our website.”
Michael Kors
FoundIt! reports that Michael Kors has gone live with its technology. In doing so, the luxury brand says that it has found a solution that solves its discovery challenge and keeps customers exploring when they land on its website.
FoundIt!’s VisNav is automatically guiding customers across the brand's catalogue, with experiences updated nightly to reflect changing shopper intent. When shoppers land directly on a product page from outside (where bounce rates typically reach 65%+), VisNav steps in at the top of the page to keep them engaged and help them find what they're actually looking for.
In a LinkedIn post, Chris Dunn, COO and Co-founder at FoundIt!, said: "What makes this launch especially exciting is the opportunity to help shoppers pick up their journey exactly where they are...turning a product page landing into a more relevant discovery path through the range. A brilliant collaboration with the Michael Kors team, and a great example of navigation doing more than getting people around a site: helping them discover what they came for."
He added: "It's navigation driven commerce in action: Helping customers on their missions; Improving discovery across their product range; Creating navigation that matches shopper intent; Keeping visitors on site when their entry point isn't quite right."
Michael Kors joins the likes of M&S, B&Q, John Lewis, Neiman Marcus, and Saks, who are using FoundIt! to enhance how customers navigate and discover products.

By tapping into Uber’s nationwide delivery network, we can make this experience even more convenient, particularly in moments when saving a trip matters most.”

items.body:
Do you like numbers? Do you like retail tech news? Then this is the article for you. Including Amazon Now, Rohlik Group, REWE Group, Ikea UK, Vusion, Pricer, Fermat, New Era, AliExpress, InPost, Tesco, Jysk, and Enactor.
30...Unless you've been living in a cave for the past few weeks, you'll be aware that Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto 6 is released in the UK this week, ending a 13-year wait for a new instalment of the blockbuster game.
The game, where players can explore a fictional US state called Leonida, features the series' first playable female protagonist in a 3D setting. And it has bagged stellar reviews, with the likes of The Guardian awarding it five stars and raving, "Rockstar has created the most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world that we have yet seen".
In an online post, Rockstar said: "We are sorry for adding additional time to what we realise has been a long wait, but these extra months will allow us to finish the game with the level of polish you have come to expect and deserve."
"We want to thank you again for your patience and support. While the wait is a little longer, we are incredibly excited for players to experience the sprawling state of Leonida and a return to modern day Vice City."
If, after the long wait for release day, you're in no mood to wait any longer, Amazon Now has you covered.
In a LinkedIn post, Elisa Michelin Salomon, Senior Manager, EU Amazon Now at Amazon, said: "GTA VI. At your door in 30 minutes. Grand Theft Auto VI is now available for 30-minute delivery on Amazon Now in London, Manchester and Birmingham. Need it? Now it. Go check it out on Amazon Now!"
23,200...European online grocery delivery and retail technology firm, Rohlik Group, has officially opened a new site in Opatovice nad Labem, Czech Republic, its largest building thus far.
The 23,200 m² site brings together a 7,500 m² fulfilment centre and a 15,700 m² distribution centre, creating new capacity and capabilities for its Czech operations. It will support up to 1,500 job roles and will support the gradual expansion of Express and three-hour delivery services across Hradec Králové, Pardubice and the surrounding areas.
A Rohlik Group spokesperson says: "There’s a lot that goes into getting a site like this up and running. A huge well done to everyone who has been involved in making Opatovice happen - from the teams who planned and built the operation to those now running it day to day."
1,650...InPost reports a milestone with Tesco, installing its 1,650th locker across the grocery giant's UK estate to become its largest network with any single retail partner in the UK.
According to InPost's customer research, 66% of its locker users combine their visit with a Tesco shop and 53% now visit the retailer more often because of the locker. Satisfaction is high too, with 75% of users saying their visit was more convenient because of the locker, with the majority rating the service ten out of ten and stating they would recommend it to a friend or colleague.
The milestone builds on a partnership with Tesco that began in 2021, with InPost lockers now installed across the retailer's different store formats, from Express to Extra and Superstores.
43% of Americans who shop online plan to buy themselves a gift this holiday season and are setting aside an average of $262 for self-gifting, according to a new survey from AliExpress conducted by Talker Research.
A study of 2,000 US online shoppers also found that people are focused on value and a stress free shopping experience, with free shipping, easy returns and refunds, and reliable delivery tracking among their top priorities.
With Black Friday rapidly approaching, AliExpress also announced that it is extending its annual 11.11 Global Shopping Festival through to 3rd December. Originally launched in 2009 as a day for single people to treat themselves to a gift, it has grown over the years into one of the world’s largest annual shopping events.
IMRG, a UK e-commerce association which tracks online retail performance across more than £30 billion of online spend from 230 retailers, analysed beauty advent calendar performance among its top 15 beauty retailers that sell these products. 14 of the 15 retailers recorded positive WoW revenue growth in the week their calendar was released.
Earlier launches were associated with the strongest uplift, suggesting retailers may benefit from getting in front of shoppers before the market becomes more crowded with Christmas campaigns. Beauty retailers launching before 15 September saw a +97.2% WoW revenue increase, compared with +47% among late-September launches and +53.1% in early October.
The uplift was strongest among mid-sized beauty retailers, at +140% WoW, compared with +21.7% among larger beauty retailers with turnover above £100 million.
At an average price of £180, beauty advent calendars cost more than four times the £40 average beauty basket value. Release week ABV increased by +20.8% WoW, with some beauty retailers seeing increases of more than £80.
Beauty only retailers also outperformed multi-category retailers. Revenue growth was +84.8% compared with +69.1%, while ABV growth was +38% compared with +15% - differences of 15.7 and 23 percentage points respectively.
7...REWE Group is ending its Pick & Go autonomous store project. The German retailer has been working on this with Trigo since 2021, tapping computer vision cameras to enable people to shop and go and not have to deal with traditional checkouts.
In a LinkedIn post, REWE Group's Chief Digital & Technology Officer, Christoph Eltze, said: "The future of checkout is not determined by a single technology. A large supermarket has different requirements than a small convenience location or a local supply service. And our customers also have different needs depending on the purchase. That's why we have been testing a wide variety of technological solutions and store concepts for years: from self-checkout and automated checkout processes to largely autonomous stores."
He added: "Our standard is not whether a technology is particularly new or spectacular. What matters is whether it makes shopping easier for our customers and proves itself in real operation. Testing is therefore an essential part of our self-understanding. With clear learning objectives and openness to different outcomes. Because not every test has to be continued exactly as it started. What matters is what we can learn from it and use elsewhere."
In seven Pick & Go test markets in Germany, REWE Group tested computer vision in a day to day store environment over a long period of time. In doing so, it says that it learned a lot about how customers use automated checkout and what requirements the technology must meet in daily operations.
Eltze commented: "We have achieved the learning objectives we set for ourselves in advance. That is precisely why the operational testing phase in these seven markets is now ending, and the evaluation of the insights gained is beginning to decide what further developments we can derive from them."
"What is important to me is that the end of this testing phase is not the end of our engagement with computer vision. On the contrary. We also further test and develop various applications and concepts for automated and autonomous shopping elsewhere. Because it's not about finding a technology for the future of checkout. The goal is to find out which solution offers our customers the greatest added value in which purchasing situation. That's why we test. That's what we learn for. And from that, we continue to develop. This is exactly how reliable decisions are made for tomorrow's trade."
SEK 980.4 million...VusionGroup, a specialist in digitalisation solutions for physical retail, has announced a recommended public takeover offer to acquire all shares in electronic shelf labels big hitter Pricer for SEK 6.00 in cash per share, valuing the company at approximately SEK 980.4 million.
According to a press release, the deal would bring together "two pioneers of electronic shelf labelling solutions, giving Pricer's customers access to a broader range of technology solutions to improve store performance, further digitalise their stores and enhance the customer experience."
The offer has been approved by Vusion's board of directors, whilst Pricer's board of directors has recommended that the company's shareholders accept it.
The acceptance period is expected to commence on or around 8th December and expire on or around 5th January, subject to any extensions. Settlement is set to start on 12th January.
"We are excited by the prospect of bringing together two European pioneers in this sector. Pricer has developed a fantastic customer portfolio of great pioneering retailers across the world and we will put the full strength of our solutions at their service to further improve store performance and the shopping experience," says Thierry Gadou, Chairman and CEO at Vusion.
"Vusion is a key player in store digitalisation solutions with a well established technology platform. We are encouraged by their recognition of the value of Pricer's business, reflected in an offer that provides our shareholders the opportunity to realise the value we have built. The proposed combination could also give our customers access to a broader portfolio of solutions. We are enthusiastic about this opportunity," says Magnus Larsson, President and CEO at Pricer.
£2.26 billion...Ikea UK has announced retail sales of £2.26 billion for financial year 2026 (FY26), an increase of 0.5% compared with the previous year (£2.25 billion).
The retailer says that its expanded store footprint helped deliver a strong start to the year, with sales revenue growing 4.7% year-on-year in the first four months of FY26. However, a challenging trading environment with weakened consumer confidence and sustained pressure on household budgets saw sales revenue dip in the second half of the year.
David McCabe, CEO and CSO at Ikea UK&IE, says: “I’m incredibly proud that in extremely challenging market conditions, we’ve managed to close financial year 2026 in growth. In a year when many households continued to manage their budgets carefully, we saw just how important the home remains to people’s everyday lives. This growth reflects the trust people place in Ikea to offer quality, sustainable and well designed home furnishing solutions at prices as low as possible."
“In September, we started financial year 2027 with a clear priority: to continue giving customers the best possible value for money at a time when every pound matters. While cost of living pressures continue, we know a well-functioning home can make a real difference to everyday life. That’s why we’re continuing to invest in lowering our prices, helping more people create the home they want at a price they can afford.”
$8 million...Fermat, a Barcelona-based AI platform for the fashion industry, has raised $8 million in seed funding to open a New York office and expand its software from a design tool to full garment production.
To begin, the company, which launched in 2022, is launching Techpacks, a tool which turns designs into factory ready specifications.
The seed round was led by Kibo Ventures and Lunar Ventures, with participation from London-based PROfounders Capital, whose combined portfolios include companies such as Unity, Flywire, Job&Talent and Zama. Other participating investors include Masia Ventures, Blue Wire Capital, Common Magic, Betaworks and tech entrepreneur Dídac Lee.
Fermat is used by more than 350 customers across 14 countries, including Asos, J.Crew Group, New Look, S. Oliver, and Tendam, with designers tapping the platform to integrate AI into existing product development workflows.
6...New Era has opened a flagship UK store on London's Oxford Street. This is its sixth location in the capital.
In a LinkedIn post, New Era's Natalie Defries said: "We're thrilled to announce that our new store at 386 Oxford Street, London W1C 1JT is now open, on the UK's busiest shopping street. Delivered in partnership with CM Delta, it marks another big step in our retail expansion across the region."
Across more than 117m² and three floors, the store offers: Ground floor: a curated selection of the brand's key silhouettes, plus a dedicated area for product exclusive to Oxford Street; Basement: a broader seasonal range of headwear and apparel, centred around a permanent customisation space offering embroidery and exclusive custom designed store patches; First floor: dedicated entirely to the 59FIFTY, in a bespoke environment with an additional customisation station
500...Vusion, a specialist in AI powered digitalisation solutions for physical retail, has been named one of TIME’s World’s Best Companies - Sustainable Growth 2027, ranking at the 51st position.
The list highlights 500 companies worldwide that combine revenue growth and financial stability with strong environmental performance.
“Being named among TIME’s World’s Best Companies for Sustainable Growth 2027 is a significant recognition of our team’s commitment to creating lasting value through both business performance and sustainability,” says Pascale Dubreuil, Chief Sustainability Officer, Vusion.
“Through intelligent, connected, and durable digital solutions, we help retailers accelerate their transition toward data driven, low carbon, and circular operations. This recognition validates our belief that Vusion’s technology can deliver a compelling combination of financial and environmental value, enabling customers to improve efficiency, profitability, and sustainability simultaneously.”
2,200...Jysk reports completion of an important step in its unified commerce journey. All of the retailer's stores in the Netherlands, Belgium, the UK and Ireland are now operating on a new platform powered by Enactor.
With these four countries fully onboard, more than 2,200 Jysk stores have gone live on the platform.
"Our store colleagues are already seeing the benefits," says Melissa Hessing, Store Manager at Jysk Alkmaar. “We moved through it very quickly. The checkout system is very user-friendly and largely self-explanatory. It will be especially easy for new colleagues."
"The implementation has been an exciting and busy process, filled with training, learning and valuable discussions about new ways of working. And there is no doubt that unified commerce will bring significant benefits to our customers, our stores and our colleagues."

items.title: Expert tips to the best Black Friday deals: Leave items in your basket for 48 hours but only buy on the day - and how to tell if old models are BETTER than the latest
items.summary: Black Friday is just a week away with huge deals on offer for savvy shoppers on November 27. But you'll need to keep your wits about you to spot the genuine deals.
items.body:
Expert tips to the best Black Friday deals: Leave items in your basket for 48 hours but only buy on the day - and how to tell if old models are BETTER than the latest
By TOBY WALNE, CHIEF MONEY REPORTER
Updated:
Black Friday is just a week away with huge deals on offer for savvy shoppers on November 27.
But you’ll need to keep your wits about you to spot the genuine deals – every year there are countless offers that are not nearly as generous as they first appear.
Here our experts share their SEVEN techniques to bag a genuine bargain.
Calculate good deals in advance
Retailers often boast of huge Black Friday price reductions, but not all are genuine. In some cases, prices are elevated just ahead of Black Friday so that retailers can cut them and claim they are offering a good deal. In others, prices drop even lower after Black Friday.
The consumer group Which? found that eight in ten of the 200 Black Friday deals it looked into last year could be found cheaper or at the same price at other times of the year.
Analysis by Money Mail also found that online retailers, such as Temu, which advertised more than 50 per cent off selected Black Friday ‘lightning deal’ items last year, were selling the same items for the same lower price 30 days previously.
To make sure you’re not falling for these tricks, check the price history of items before you hit ‘buy’.
Retailers often boast of huge Black Friday price reductions – but not all of them are genuine
The website CamelCamelCamel.com offers price history for items sold on Amazon. You can search by item to show the price charged over months or even years.
For example, it shows that the Ninja AutoBarista Automatic Espresso Machine cost £799 on Amazon through July and August, but the price started to fall in early September. It is now for sale at the lowest price seen at £599. There is no knowing if the price will drop lower on Black Friday, but at least if you buy at this price you know it’s the lowest yet.
You could even come up with a shopping list in advance for items that you genuinely want, noting down the price for each that you think would represent a good discount.
Having a prepared list also helps to counter the tricks by retailers designed to make you spend more on impulse.
Janina Steinmetz, a professor in marketing at Bayes Business School in London, says: ‘Black Friday creates time pressure which can make you respond in a more impulsive way than usual. It can mean buying something that is not such a great bargain or items you don’t need.’
Laura Turner, a personal finance blogger and social media influencer, says: ‘Shops may have put up prices to make the Black Friday discounts look more compelling – but do not be lured in without finding the usual prices.’
Wait until the day itself
Black Friday is an idea imported from retailers in the United States and falls on the day after Thanksgiving. The idea is traders sell enough to get back into the ‘black’ – after spending much of the year in the red and losing money because they have failed to attract enough shoppers at other times. Some retailers launch sales on the day itself, while others start earlier.
Among the first out of the blocks were Argos, Boots and Currys, which started offering Black Friday discounts at the end of October. Others, including online shops AO and Very, plus high street chains Halfords, Robert Dyas and Superdrug, have also started their sales. Amazon is expected to offer Black Friday deals in the week of the big day, as are Debenhams and John Lewis.
Other major retailers such as Apple, Asos and Waterstones are not expected to launch their sales until the day. The shops involved in Black Friday typically keep their offers open throughout the weekend until at least Monday – which is known as Cyber Monday.
While it may be tempting to get shopping as soon as the sales begin, sometimes even better discounts are offered on the day itself.
Consumer expert Martyn James says: ‘Patience is the way forward – shops are trying to manipulate you by creating a buzz so you spend more. A discount could drop even further on the day so stand firm and do not panic.
‘But online buyers can still put items in the basket now if they are worried about forgetting the great deal. They can then press the “buy now” button on the Friday to pick up this same deal – or get an even better offer.’
Ms Turner also believes that if you want the biggest discounts you should wait for the big day.
She says: ‘Some clothes shops are already offering 30 per cent off discounts. But there might be a flash sale of a further 20 per cent off to create a half price offer on the day. My only warning is if stocks run low and sales items run out early.’
Consumer expert Martyn James says that ‘online buyers can put items in the basket now if they are worried about forgetting the great deal’
Use tools to trawl the market for you
Shopping around to get the best deal is crucial – even when there are Black Friday discounts on offer. However, you don’t have to trawl around online retailers to price compare – use a specialist website to do it for you. For example, PriceRunner, Idealo and Google Shopping all allow you to search for a particular item and see the prices offered by various retailers listed in one place.
Ms Turner, who runs the popular lifestyle Instagram account @bylauraturner, says: ‘You need a sharp eye when comparing offers but fortunately the internet can do much of the work. Also take advantage of price matching at stores such as John Lewis. It offers to price match against 25 competitors.’
Mr James says: ‘Rather than hovering over the buy-now button when shopping online you can also put a sales item in the shopping basket and simply leave it there for up to 48 hours. You may find the retailer contacts you during this time and offers a bigger discount. I have heard instances when luxury shops have offered an extra 25 per cent off to bag a sale.’
Sign up to cashback for your shopping
With cashback websites such as TopCashback and Quidco, you receive extra money on top of the prices you pay for items.
Ms Turner says: ‘Using cashback websites alongside Black Friday discounts makes your money work twice as hard – and is a habit you must get into.’
To start you need to sign up to the cashback website for free to get the deal – with your name, email address and a password. Then visit shops through the website to find your Black Friday discounts. You can check different cashback providers to ensure you get the best reward.
The cashback websites earn a small commission from the retailer for directing you to them, while you pick up a reward, typically 3 to 10 per cent of a purchase price. This reward is put automatically into your online cashback account and can be paid in vouchers.
Watch out for older models
Jasmine Birtles, founder of consumer website Money Magpie, says that in some cases retailers are offering discounts to sell off older models – particularly in the case of electronic gadgets – to make way for newer releases.
This needn’t put you off – many shoppers do not need the most recent model and are happy to have the lower price. But if the age of a model matters to you, you may want to check if there is a new one coming out shortly before purchasing.
‘It is all about research beforehand,’ she adds.
Jasmine Birtles, founder of consumer website Money Magpie, says that ‘research beforehand’ can help in snagging deals on older models of electronic gadgets
Buy online if you want time to change your mind
When buying online, under the Consumer Contracts Regulations you have a 14-day cooling off period that starts from the day of receiving your goods – during which time you can cancel or return the goods for any reason.
However, you do not have the same right if you buy in person.
Some high street shops will only accept returns on sales goods if an item is faulty – not if you have changed your mind. Under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, goods must be of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose and as described. So, always check the terms and conditions with a retailer before your purchase, and be polite if you want to return goods as it may be at the shop’s discretion.
You have 30 days to claim if you need a repair, replacement or refund. If goods were bought within six months you are entitled to a single repair or replacement. However, you may not get the same amount that you paid for it because a refund need only reflect a current price.
Mr James says: ‘Waking up the next morning feeling buyers’ regret is something you can solve with ease. You may have saved money on the purchase, but you will be a lot better off if you simply return the item for a refund.’
Be sure to use a genuine website
In all the excitement of snapping up a bargain before it sells out, you could stumble on a bogus copycat website that aims to trick you into thinking it is genuine.
Criminals take advantage of events such as Black Friday because if you make a panicked decision, you are less likely to take time to check the website is legitimate.
Scammers often clone designs of retail shops, pretending to be boutique outfits that need your business. Telltale signs to look out for are unusual suffixes, such as .top, .co, .xyz and .cc to imitate a real co.uk or .com site. The website can also have spelling or grammatical mistakes.
A secure website starts with ‘https’ in the address and has a padlock symbol on the address bar of your internet browser.
If you are spending more than £100 it is recommended to use a credit card as this provides legal protection if the company goes bust, items do not arrive or there are other problems, such as being scammed.
Ms Birtles says: ‘Try to ignore the emails and texts from retailers announcing Black Friday deals because, sadly, it is easy for scammers to create these and take you to a false website where you can get cheated out of money.’

items.title: Tens of thousands of UK fridges secured from hackers in secret nationwide operation
items.summary: Supermarkets, warehouses, restaurants and stadiums have been scrambling to make their devices safe.
items.body:
Tens of thousands of UK fridges secured from hackers in secret nationwide operation
- Published
A behind the scenes cyber-security operation has taken place to secure tens of thousands of fridges and freezers at major UK supermarkets, warehouses, restaurants, petrol stations and stadiums from hackers, the BBC has learned.
Recent waves of cyber-attacks in Europe have seen tonnes of food spoiled at hundreds of stores, causing millions of pounds of damage.
France has blamed Iran for one of the waves of attacks that impacted its supermarkets, a claim Tehran denies.
It was thought the UK had largely escaped such hacks as the British refrigeration industry relies on different devices but there was in fact a potential vulnerability the sector has been rushing to fix.
In late October, security researchers discovered a major flaw that, if found by hackers, could have led to even worse damage to the UK.
Since then, researchers, IT teams and the National Cyber Security Centre have been working around the clock to warn dozens of companies.
The BBC has not reported on the large-scale, secretive operation until now to reduce the chances of hackers causing harm if they found the vulnerability.
Thousands of fridges taken off-line
The security threat was discovered by staff at refrigeration consultants Omega Solutions - it was then verified and expanded upon by experts at Pen Test Partners who helped raise the alarm.
The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), the Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs (Defra) and Food Standards Agency (FSA) were then involved in the campaign to plug the security holes.
They held industry conference calls and tasked teams to contact firms at risk.
Thousands of devices controlling tens of thousands of refrigeration devices were taken off the open internet either remotely or, in some cases, physically - with staff ordered to remove internet cables and monitor temperatures manually.
BBC news has learnt most major supermarkets have been forced to divert IT teams to address the risks, with a worker at one large chain saying they took hundreds of devices offline every day over the course of a week.
"It did feel like a race against time as we were expecting another wave of these fridge hacks to come," said the person, who did not want to be publicly named.
"From a business perspective it could have been potentially devastating with business interruption and supply chain problems. Our warehouses have millions of pounds worth of food that could have been spoiled if any hackers found out about this method of attack," they added.
There have been three waves of hacks on refrigeration temperature controllers so far this year:
- In August, fridges at a small number of US military bases were impacted
- On 11 and 12 October hundreds of supermarkets and food processing sites in France were hit when Danfoss temperature control systems were targeted
- On 1 and 2 November dozens of supermarkets across seven European countries were hit, with Belgium and Luxembourg the worst affected. A small number of blood bank sites in France were also impacted
The waves of attacks prompted an expert at Omega Solutions to examine the security of the most popular refrigeration controllers in the UK, made by British firm Resource Data Management (RDM).
RDM disputes the critical nature of the vulnerabilities exposed but has been praised for its professional response to address the concerns, the BBC understands.
As well as supermarkets, multiple other areas of UK food and beverage industry were also warned to take action about the risks.
These include convenience stores, petrol stations, restaurants and fast food chains, sports arenas, hotels, food processing plants and cold storage sites.
"These popular controllers had a similar weak password problem to the Danfoss and other controllers that were attacked so successfully in previous hacks so we had to get the message out as soon as possible and keep it secret," said Ken Munro of Pen Test Partners.
"There is so much extra attention on these ubiquitous bits of kit now that it was likely a matter of days until criminals or nation state hackers figured it out," he added.
RDM, though, says comparisons with the units attacked in mainland Europe are not fair because hacking their fridges and freezers would have involved getting hold of a piece of hardware.
The ethical hackers say this would have been achievable as the hardware in question can be purchased cheaply online on sites like eBay.
"This was a vulnerability identified in a test environment," said Ged Evans, CEO of RDM.
He said the test "went beyond" what such exercises usually involved, as it "included dismantling our hardware".
"In any event we have acted at pace to address this issue and have already deployed first patch releases and have been in proactive contact with our customers to flag any issues and recommend mitigatory steps," he added.
RDM confirmed that there was no sign of any malicious activity on the controllers and that it continued to work with the NCSC and other authorities to monitor the situation.

items.title: JD Sports slashes profit forecasts as French riot looting damages shops and hits sales
items.summary: The self-described 'King of Trainers' said it now expects annual profits to be between £700m and £750m, compared with a previous range of £700m to £800m.
items.body:
JD Sports slashes profit forecasts as French riot looting damages shops and hits sales
JD Sports slashed its profit forecasts after French riots hit sales.
The shoes and sportswear retailer expects annual profits to be between £700million and £750million, compared with a previous range of £700million to £800million.
Chief executive Regis Schultz said trading in Europe had been ‘affected by civil unrest’ in France over the cost of living and quality of education.
Its shops in Orleans and Nice were looted, and Schultz said these especially hurt sales, though staff’s ‘courage, professionalism and resilience have been outstanding’.
Group revenue was £2.9billion in the 13 weeks to October 31 – a 2.6 per cent drop in same-store sales.
In the UK, cooler weather last month helped boost sales of autumn/winter ranges that had been ‘delayed by unseasonably warm weather’, but like-for-like sales still fell 2.6 per cent.
A looted branch of JD Sports in Paris, France, following riots linked to protests over the cost-of-living and school funding in October
The retailer, which often collaborates with TV personalities such as Maya Jama, has been struggling in recent years as its young consumer base is squeezed by economic pressures.
Shares tumbled 4.3 per cent, or 4.02p, to 90.3p yesterday.
In the UK, cooler weather last month helped to boost sales of autumn/winter ranges that had been ‘delayed by unseasonably warm weather earlier in the quarter,’ the group said. Like-for-like sales still fell 2.6 per cent.
The High Street retailer, which often collaborates with TV personalities such as Maya Jama, has been struggling in recent years as its young consumer base is squeezed by economic pressures.
Its trading has also been affected by a downturn faced by Nike, which makes up around 45 per cent of its sales.
The trainer giant has seen its sales nibbled at by trendier challenger brands such as On and Hoka amid a running boom.
The retailer, which has 4,681 stores across 31 countries, last cut profit guidance just in August when it cut its range from between £750million to £850million.
Schultz said: ‘Our multi-brand, multi-category model keeps us agile and quick to respond to changing customer trends and demand.
‘We are raising the bar on our product ranges, bringing new launches to market faster, particularly in apparel, and investing in a stronger, more seamless experience across stores and online.’
Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, said: ‘JD needs a radical shift in the athleisure world, where hype around new product launches drives customers into its shops and onto its website.
‘The tills should keep ringing from people needing the essentials, yet there is no buzz about the brand.
'Either JD or one of its key suppliers needs to have a major marketing breakthrough, otherwise the retailer will be running hard just to stand still.’

items.title: Suspects charged in California train heist ring that netted cargo worth $22m
items.summary: More than a dozen people allegedly targeted trains carrying Nike sneakers, Crocs footwear and other goods More than a dozen people were charged on Thursday with allegedly orchestrating a vast train heist operation to steal more than $22m in cargo – from popular shoes to power tools – from major retailers . A federal indictment unsealed on Thursday paints a picture of an organized group that targeted more than three dozen trains carrying Nike sneakers, Crocs footwear, power tools and other consumer goods that were imported into the United States through Los Angeles and Long Beach, which are home to the busiest ports in the country. Continue reading...
items.body:
More than a dozen people were charged on Thursday with allegedly orchestrating a vast train heist operation to steal more than $22m in cargo – from popular shoes to power tools – from major retailers.
A federal indictment unsealed on Thursday paints a picture of an organized group that targeted more than three dozen trains carrying Nike sneakers, Crocs footwear, power tools and other consumer goods that were imported into the United States through Los Angeles and Long Beach, which are home to the busiest ports in the country.
Trains that shuttle goods to stores and customers around the country have become a prominent target for large-scale theft in recent years, especially at large ports in the US that receive hundreds of millions of dollars of shipments every day. The relatively low-tech robberies have demanded attention from the world’s largest retailers, including the likes of Amazon.
The men would disable the trains at a planned location by busting the brakes, the indictment alleged, at which point the goods would be offloaded on to trucks. The goods were then peddled to an unnamed company that would resell the stolen merchandise for profit.
“The scale of the theft is staggering,” said first assistant United States attorney Bill Essayli, promising to prosecute any future efforts to steal the merchandise.
In group chats, the men shared numerous photos and videos of themselves busting into the hulking train cars, and posing with wads of cash and stolen merchandise. They also shared AI photos of themselves captioned “Los Trenes”, which means the trains in Spanish, beneath glamorized photos of men throwing boxes of shoes off trains into nearby cars while police helicopters descended overhead.
The 13 men were indicted for conspiracy and theft of interstate railroad cargo. Two were also charged with violence against railroad carriers.
If convicted, the men could face anywhere from five to 20 years in federal prison.

items.body:
Hotel Chocolat has launched an AI-powered Gift Assistant on its website, giving customers a new way to choose thoughtful gifts this Christmas. The assistant emulates the conversation a customer might have with a colleague in one of its shops. Customers can describe who they’re buying for, refine the recommendations through follow-up questions and add their chosen gift to their basket within the same experience.
The launch comes as AI becomes an established part of the shopping journey, with Adobe research finding that 37% of UK consumers now use AI assistants to shop. Hotel Chocolat is responding to that shift by giving customers a way to ask for ideas in their own words directly on its website, starting with a decision its store teams help customers make every day.
The Gift Assistant builds on Hotel Chocolat’s wider Christmas campaign, which starts with the person receiving the gift. A customer could ask, “find me a dark chocolate Christmas gift”. The assistant would then ask a follow-up question and refine the shortlist as the customer shares more. From there, the customer can explore product details, choose from available pack sizes and gifting options, and add their selection to their basket.
Hotel Chocolat worked with Astound Digital and Salesforce to turn conversational search into a shoppable experience. Salesforce Agentforce and Cimulate’s semantic search capability interpret a customer’s request and match it to product data in Salesforce Commerce Cloud. A customer can start with “a thank-you for a host who loves dark chocolate”, refine the recommendations by adding a budget, then choose from available gifting options and add their selection to their basket within the same experience.
Martin Bell, digital director at Hotel Chocolat, said: “Search is becoming more conversational, and that’s changing what customers expect from a retailer’s website. We wanted to be on the front foot and make hotelchocolat.com a place people come for expert advice, inspiration and the confidence to choose a gift that feels right. In 11 weeks, together with Astound and Salesforce, we transformed the website experience with our new Gift Assistant, in time for our busiest gifting period. That means we can learn from real Christmas shopping decisions by seeing what people ask for, which recommendations they act on and where they still need help. What we learn will shape how we use conversational AI across Hotel Chocolat, including how we help customers discover our products when their search starts beyond our website.”
Emma Sahota, managing director UKI at Astound Digital, said: “The future of commerce isn’t just about helping customers find products faster; it’s about helping them make better decisions. By harnessing AI, Hotel Chocolat is bringing the expertise of its in-store teams into the online shopping journey, making gifting more intuitive, personal and effortless. It’s a great example of what’s possible when retailers combine a clear customer vision with the right technology and delivery expertise, creating a strong foundation for continued innovation.”
Hotel Chocolat will use the Christmas trading period to assess how the assistant shapes product discovery. Those findings will inform further functionality planned for early 2027 and the business’s wider strategy for large language models (LLMs).
Explore and experience the new AI gift assistant here: https://www.hotelchocolat.com/uk/gift-assistant

items.title: B&M accuses Morrisons of ‘concerted’ poaching campaign to dupe products
items.summary: Discount retailer B&M has accused Morrisons of a “concerted campaign” to poach its staff and “flagrantly” copy its products, City AM can reveal. London-listed B&M is pursuing court action against the supermarket giant over claims it poached eight of its employees to help it “copy” scores of its products, including Halloween-themed decorations and “cosy season” [...]
items.body:
B&M accuses Morrisons of ‘concerted’ poaching campaign to dupe products
Discount retailer B&M has accused Morrisons of a “concerted campaign” to poach its staff and “flagrantly” copy its products, City AM can reveal.
London-listed B&M is pursuing court action against the supermarket giant over claims it poached eight of its employees to help it “copy” scores of its products, including Halloween-themed decorations and “cosy season” accessories.
In High Court filings, seen by City AM, the discount retailer alleges Morrisons orchestrated a “longstanding, deliberate and concerted campaign” against B&M which has caused it “substantial and irreparable loss and damage”.
The retailer has accused the supermarket chain of “copying exactly or substantially” a number of products in its Halloween and “cosy season” ranges.
The products in this line include scented candles, doormats, faux fur throws, duvet covers, decorative books and glass vases.
B&M’s accusations centre on Simon Buckley, against whom it is also pursuing legal action. Buckley worked at B&M for more than 14 years, eventually as its director of merchandising, before joining Morrisons as its trading director in January this year.
B&M claims Buckley breached the terms of his contract with the retailer by holding talks with Morrisons while he was still on gardening leave, after leaving B&M in September.
The retailer also alleges Buckley breached its confidence and broke trade secrets rules by sharing “cheat sheets” with Morrisons employees which it claims included details of its bestselling Halloween and gardening products.
‘Flagrant’ copyright breaches
In its court filings, B&M lists seven employees in its buying and products departments who quit the retailer to join Morrisons in the months after Buckley quit.
It is “inherently likely” that Buckley “solicited the employment of those individuals, suggested that the First Defendant [Morrisons] hire those individuals” and “induced or enticed” them away from B&M, it claims.
The discount retailer added that it thinks Morrisons plans to continue plagiarising its products. The supermarket has continued to “advertise, promote and sell” these items since it was first told in October that they were copied, it claims.
B&M is seeking damages for Morrisons’s “flagrant” alleged breaches of intellectual property.
This is not the first time retailers come under scrutiny for alleged plagiarism. Toymaker Jellycat has pursued a number of high street firms in recent months for making so-called dupes, including Home Bargains, Morrisons and Next.
A spokesperson for Morrisons said: “While we will not be commenting in detail as court proceedings have now been commenced by B&M, we do not accept the merits of their claim and will be fully defending it.”
The former B&M employees named in the lawsuit were contacted for comment.
A B&M spokesperson said: “B&M has commenced legal proceedings against Morrisons in relation to allegations of intellectual property infringement and breach of confidence.
“We invest significantly in developing our products and protecting our confidential business information and will take appropriate action where we believe those rights have been infringed.
“As the matter is now before the courts, it would not be appropriate to comment further.”

The award-winning Eat 17 in Walthamstow has joined the wholesaler on a new five-year contract as a “Proud to Stock Co-op” partner.
With a focus on premium lines throughout, the store owners aim to focus on Co-op’s Irresistible lines, from chocolate and biscuits to wine and steak, to complement its existing range of fine foods and drinks.
Ian King, Business Development and Growth Director at Co-op Wholesale, said: “We’re thrilled to welcome this unique and brilliant store as a partner to Co-op Wholesale. It’s clear to see why it’s won multiple awards.
“Our Co-op brand lines look totally at home on the shelves, especially the premium Irresistible products.”
Directors at Eat17, Chris O’Connor and James Brundle, will continue to operate the store.
O’Connor said: “Eat17 has always been about bringing great food to our local community and this partnership with Co-op Wholesale gives us the chance to offer our customers even more choice.
“The Co-op Irresistible range is a fantastic fit for the store, sitting alongside the brilliant independent producers and local favourites that make Eat17 special.
The store’s offer includes coffee and pizza that customers can enjoy on-site.

items.title: PayPoint ‘working to improve retailer service’ as profits drop
items.summary: PayPoint has reported a 13.2% drop in profit and seen its shares fall by 15% today (19 November). The payment and retail services company, which works with more than 30,000 convenience stores and shops, said it expected business to improve in the second half of… This story continues at PayPoint ‘working to improve retailer service’ as profits drop Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The payment and retail services company, which works with more than 30,000 convenience stores and shops, said it expected business to improve in the second half of the year.
The number of retail sites in which PayPoint operates has declined slightly from 30,872 stores at the end of March to 30,515 in the latest figures.
But PayPoint said its retailer service improved over the same period, with calls from retailers answered 60% faster and a third more handled each week.
A dedicated technical support team launched in September is restoring devices more quickly and also helping to proactively resolve issues before retailers call, the company claimed.
Overall, PayPoint saw its profit before tax decrease to £22.3m compared with the same period in its previous financial year, and net revenue fall to £81.9m from £84.7m.
Nevertheless, the company said it expected a full-year outcome “broadly in line with market expectations”.
Nick Wiles, chief executive, said: “Our focus in the first half has been to build on the organisational changes implemented earlier in the year, strengthening ownership, accountability and execution across our four scaled business units.
“In doing so, we have established a stronger foundation from which to deliver the growth ambitions set out at our recent capital markets day.
“Overall, the business has performed in line with expectations in the first half, with momentum building during the second quarter and resilient trading across the group as a whole.”

items.body:
Chirpy, the pharmacist-formulated youth mental wellbeing food supplement brand founded by sisters Emma Grace and Sarah Pontefract, has announced its retail debut, with The Mood One (RRP. £29.99) and The Zen One (RRP. £27.99) available online at Boots and Holland & Barrett now. Just six months after launching direct-to-consumer in May 2026, the move puts Chirpy on the digital shelves of two of the UK’s most trusted health retailers, making it easier for parents and carers to find it where they already shop, many of whom are looking for credible, science-led support for their children’s mood, sleep and focus.
Parents of children and teens who are struggling with low mood, anxious feelings, poor sleep or trouble focusing have plenty of advice to read, but few trusted places to turn for nutritional support designed specifically for young people. Chirpy was created to fill that gap: evidence-based food supplements for children and young people aged 6-18 whose mood, emotional regulation, sleep or focus suggest their brains may benefit from additional building blocks, backed by clinical research into natural ingredients shown to support mood, focus and emotional balance in adolescents.
Chirpy was founded by sisters Emma Grace, a brand marketer, and Sarah Pontefract, a pharmacist and Professor of Medicines Safety, who combine consumer brand instinct and personal story with clinical credibility. Every Chirpy food supplement is pharmacist-formulated, and the brand’s mission is simple: to build more good mood days for young minds.
The retail launches follow a fast start. Chirpy launched in May 2026 with two hero products, The Mood One and The Zen One, and sales have grown month-on-month since. A 67% subscription rate shows families are choosing to stay with the brand, and 99% of customers say they would recommend Chirpy to others.
Chirpy has also attracted high profile support. Broadcaster, best-selling author and Happy Place founder Fearne Cotton is a Chirpy shareholder and its Head of Happy, and recently fronted the brand’s Mood M.O.T. campaign, helping families check in on their children’s wellbeing habits as the days get shorter.
Behind the brand is also the Chirpy Collective, a panel of leading experts who believe in the product and the principles it is built on:
- Dr Carolyne Keenan, teen psychologist
- Jo Rodriguez, health psychologist
- Dr Rachel Gow, nutritional neuroscientist
- Dr Becky Guest, clinical psychologist
- Dr Amy Wilson, paediatrician
- Carly Williams, naturopath and yoga therapist
Together, they shape Chirpy’s approach to supporting young people’s mental wellbeing, offering free expert advice, tips and practical everyday habits to introduce via the ‘Headucation’ section of the Chirpy website.
“Parents have told us they want something credible they can find where they already shop for their family’s health,” says Emma Grace, co-founder of Chirpy. “Seeing Chirpy listed with Boots and Holland & Barrett within months of launching is a huge milestone, and it means more families can now more easily find support they trust.”
“We built Chirpy because there was nothing comparable that was made specifically for young minds, with the rigour I would expect as a pharmacist,” adds Sarah Pontefract, Pharmacist and co-Founder of Chirpy. “Working with two retailers that families already trust to support their health and wellbeing is the next step in our mission to build more good mood days for children and teenagers.”
